title: Legacy core audit: correctness work queue
text:
Independent static review, 2026-10-20. Baseline: 41bd7000363f34b1e7e2d7e354971bfe9021e2b1 (relevant implementation blobs also match 5617a6daed1f4743a9b2609694a2f84ad4c902eb). These are source findings, not reproduced runtime failures unless a later entry supplies a regression test and exact CI result. Do not infer that existing Rust behavior is a requirement.









Finding and baseline source
Required correction and evidence




Overlapping docs/output/cache paths; docs . or ancestor; symlinked parents; separator-bearing labels. yml.rs:337, clear.rs:158, fs_utils.rs:1.
Reject unsafe destructive destinations before writes; resolve identity/overlap and staging aliases; protect source/raw/root state. External resource paths remain valid. Test actual preservation with root/ancestor/overlap/traversal/symlink fixtures.


VERSION and outputs change before hooks; rollback covers only the execution middle. build.rs:236, build.rs:328.
Stage managed writes and cover hooks, snapshots, execution, postprocessing and promotion with complete error handling. Restore exact prior managed state, including VERSION absence/bytes.


Public docs cleared before ignored promotion failures; post-cleanup precedes CAS export. build.rs:359, build.rs:370, build.rs:430.
Require successful expected-output promotion and archive real output bytes before cleanup; never report success after failed/missing promotion. Preserve the previous release on failure.


Environment read errors suppressed through lines().flatten(); invalid names can panic; required files can be ignored. env.rs:69, env.rs:181.
Bounded reads, validation before mutation, explicit errors for directory/unreadable/empty/NUL inputs; prove analysis never starts.


Environment guard mutates process-wide variables across library builds. env.rs:118.
Resolve a per-run map and apply child-command environment explicitly. Overlapping projects must not exchange variables/profiles/credentials or change caller environment. A private mutex cannot protect unrelated readers.


Credential helper embeds tokens in arguments/shell text, ignores requested host and inherited-helper behavior. git.rs:146.
Prefer native configured authentication. Any override needs fixed code, exact host scope and no secret in argv/source. Use synthetic punctuation-bearing sentinels and mocked Git; never real credentials in logs.


Optional Git work runs implicitly; fetch despite disabled checks, duplicate commits, hardcoded branch and discarded token. build_pre.rs:112, build.rs final Git stages.
Execute only requested operations using real upstream/native auth; handle clean commits and separate local success from publication failure. Mock Git/network tests.













Finding and baseline source
Required correction and evidence




Literal root metacharacters become script glob syntax. build.rs:650, build.rs:681.
Escape literal root only, keep user include/exclude syntax; verify actual analysis bytes in bracket/space-named roots.


Renderer YAML rewritten persistently, malformed YAML replaced by empty mapping and restoration loses original text/keys. build.rs:709, build.rs:338.
Validate early; prefer supported renderer controls, otherwise exact-byte restoration on every exit.


Individual documents ignore configured docs destination; PDF/DOCX formats guessed as HTML; promotion errors discarded. build.rs:271, build.rs:363, build_pre.rs:79.
One validated destination and explicit supported format mapping; reject unsupported formats rather than guessing; require actual expected artifacts.


Rmd filename interpolated into executable R source. build.rs:990.
Pass data/arguments to fixed R code; test spaces, apostrophes, backslashes and Unicode without local R execution.


Remote paths stay invocation-relative and invalid content tags/errors are dropped. yml.rs:429, build.rs:435.
Normalize paths against the captured root, validate content tags before writes and propagate export failures.


CAS path normalization can collide on Unix; scan/copy race can store bytes under the wrong digest. cas.rs:202, cas.rs:248.
Preserve platform path distinctions or reject unsupported names; verify stored bytes against digest and fail on source mutation.


CAS broader integrity gaps: existing-object trust, unsafe boundaries, non-atomic manifest, CSV escaping, existence-only verification, malformed digest/path traversal and missing/file source accepted as empty snapshot.
Extend existing CAS work rather than claim a redesign is complete. Require a real input directory and fixture-backed integrity/error behavior.


Unsupported control keys silently filtered; runtime invents directory defaults/subpaths. yml.rs filtering/validation/get_path.
Enforce approved active configuration and explicit used mappings, reject unsupported behavior settings before mutations. Init alone may write defaults.






After bounded configuration fixes: destructive-path guards; complete managed-state failure/promotion handling; per-run environment; Git authentication/operation corrections; exact path/context behavior; explicit renderer checks. Each focused change needs actual Ponytail full-mode review, an independent review and remote regressions. Record implemented evidence in the compatibility log.
Managed-state restoration cannot undo arbitrary external effects of user scripts or hooks. This is not an OS sandbox or global rollback promise. No trustworthy production-release safety claim follows from preview tests or this static audit. The existing R package and thesis remain untouched.
The project already uses Rust edition 2024. Do not modernize for syntax alone. Rust 1.85 is only an MSRV candidate until the locked dependency graph is tested. Release builds should use reviewed stable Rust and --locked; add fmt, clippy and documentation checks without duplicating every matrix unnecessarily. A future fixture-backed YAML dependency migration is separate from urgent correctness fixes. At current memory pressure, no local compilation, R, Docker, Quarto build or compiling source-install is authorized; use remote tests and lightweight released binary smoke checks.

title: Build lifecycle
text:
WarningReleased workflow, bounded recovery



The figures describe the reviewed lifecycle released in 0.4.0-preview.2. The exact source and executed acceptance are linked below. This is a bounded managed-path workflow, not whole-project rollback or a security sandbox. Use sample data or a disposable project copy.

title: Build lifecycle
text:
Read the figures



Mark
Meaning




[R] Released
Implemented in 0.4.0-preview.2, within the stated limits.


[?] Open
An unresolved association; no implementation promise.



Solid arrows show the reviewed controlled order. Renderers can handle several documents as one project; arbitrary mixed-language one-by-one scheduling is not promised. Dotted connections mark an unresolved association, not an execution step.
An output build means the production proj build path. A preview means proj build-dev. Clearing here means final-output clearing, not arbitrary deletion of project files or preparation of a fresh cache.

title: Build lifecycle
text:
The three stages






%%{init: {"htmlLabels": false}}%%
flowchart TB
  classDef default fill:#f0f4f7,stroke:#637b89,color:#153b32
  linkStyle default stroke:#26343f,color:#26343f
  subgraph PRE["1 · Pre-build"]
    A["Resolve and verify basic setup"]
    B["[R] Start hooks, then remaining<br/>preparation"]
    A --> B
  end
  subgraph BUILD["2 · Build"]
    C["[R] Conditional pre-clear →<br/>ordered analysis → conditional<br/>post-clear"]
  end
  subgraph POST["3 · Post-build"]
    D["[R] Preview: end hooks and<br/>captured-state restoration; no<br/>publication"]
    E["[R] Output: promotion and<br/>enabled finalization; end hooks<br/>immediately before next-dev<br/>transition"]
  end
  B --> C
  C -->|"Preview"| D
  C -->|"Output"| E
  classDef target fill:#fff3d8,stroke:#8a5b00,color:#342600
  class A,B,C,D,E target
  style PRE fill:#f1f6f3,stroke:#a8bcb4,color:#153b32
  style BUILD fill:#f1f6f3,stroke:#a8bcb4,color:#153b32
  style POST fill:#f1f6f3,stroke:#a8bcb4,color:#153b32




Figure 1: Released overview. Open the stage details below for conditions and failure boundaries.





The key adjacency rules are deliberate: nothing runs between pre-clear and analysis, or between successful analysis and post-clear. Start hooks come after verified basic setup; end hooks come at the end, immediately before the output build’s transition to the next development version.

1. Pre-build details






NoteOpen: resolution, validation, context and start hooks











%%{init: {"htmlLabels": false}}%%
flowchart TB
  classDef default fill:#f0f4f7,stroke:#637b89,color:#153b32
  linkStyle default stroke:#26343f,color:#26343f
  A["[R] Select explicit or discovered<br/>project root"]
  B["[R] Resolve profiles and<br/>environment; merge config;<br/>settings HOW / build WHAT"]
  C["[R/T] Validate typed configuration<br/>and explicit resource mappings"]
  D["[R] Capture root, profiles,<br/>mappings, mode and active run<br/>version"]
  E["[R/T] Preflight inputs and exclusion<br/>syntax, targets, dependencies and<br/>enabled Git prerequisites"]
  F["[R] Enumerate and capture managed<br/>recovery state before controlled<br/>writes"]
  G["[R] Run configured start hooks"]
  H["[R] Complete remaining safe<br/>staging, renderer and allowed<br/>metadata preparation"]
  A --> B --> C --> D --> E --> F --> G --> H
  classDef existing fill:#e5f2ed,stroke:#146859,color:#153b32
  classDef main fill:#e7effa,stroke:#315b89,color:#183954
  classDef target fill:#fff3d8,stroke:#8a5b00,color:#342600
  class A,F existing
  class D main
  class B,C,E,G,H target




Figure 2: Released pre-build order.






Root selection, effective profiles, merged configuration and environment must agree before analysis starts. The target assigns HOW choices to settings and WHAT is selected/run to build; this is not permission to add unknown fields to the installed preview.
The captured context fixes resource identity and the active run version. In the released implementation, preview retains an existing dev version or uses dev1 of a release without writing VERSION; an output run uses its requested release version throughout the run and leaves the subsequent dev1 only on success.
Validate declared paths, script/hook include and exclusion syntax, supported renderer plans, dependencies and explicitly enabled Git actions before controlled build writes. Probes can have their own effects: this is not a blanket read-only/environment sanitization guarantee. The malformed-exclusion correction is current-source work newer than preview.2; it fails in this preflight stage, without changing stage order or recovery scope. Current-source fallback directory/entry errors also stop here. The recovery capture stage reports its own enumeration phase and OS cause before controlled project writes. These diagnostics are newer than preview.2; ordering is unchanged.
Start/end refer to the existing pre/both and post/both hook sets, not new hook types. Their placement follows the controlled lifecycle shown here.
Recovery capture must precede hooks and managed mutations. Cache/staging setup, supported renderer preparation and permitted metadata/ignore work finish before the final pre-clear gate. No new metadata/provenance record is implied here.
A script’s working directory is separate from project identity. Native cwd with an explicit project override, safe resource targets and render-context path presentation are included in preview.2.






2. Build details






NoteOpen: exact clearing position and selected execution











%%{init: {"htmlLabels": false}}%%
flowchart TB
  classDef default fill:#f0f4f7,stroke:#637b89,color:#153b32
  linkStyle default stroke:#26343f,color:#26343f
  A{"Analysis selected?"}
  B{"Output build, promotion enabled<br/>and clear stage pre?"}
  C["[R] Pre-clear final outputs"]
  D["[R] Execute ordered scripts /<br/>supported renderer plan"]
  E{"Output build, promotion enabled<br/>and clear stage post?"}
  F["[R] Post-clear final outputs"]
  G["Continue to post-build"]
  N["[R/T] No analysis: skip renderer<br/>setup, analysis cleanup and<br/>execution"]
  X["Failure branch: stop success-only<br/>work and use bounded recovery"]
  A -->|"Yes"| B
  A -->|"Explicit empty list"| N --> G
  B -->|"Yes"| C --> D
  B -->|"No"| D
  D -->|"Success"| E
  D -->|"Failure"| X
  E -->|"Yes"| F --> G
  E -->|"No"| G
  classDef target fill:#fff3d8,stroke:#8a5b00,color:#342600
  class C,D,F,N target




Figure 3: Released clearing adjacency. The diamond checks select a branch; they are not extra lifecycle work.





Preview skips both final-output clear operations, even if an output setting asks for them. With scripts: [], hooks can still run and an output build may export existing artifacts; that is not proof of complete analysis-free retry identity.
The target routes eligible safe output/data roles and rendered docs through an explicitly selected versioned cache, keeping configured final destinations separate. Inputs retain their declared meaning; no undeclared docs or cache mapping is invented. Ordinary scripts can still write elsewhere: path helpers and staging are not automatic isolation of every write.
The selected execution order must follow the supported plan. Do not infer arbitrary mixed-renderer ordering or RStudio/Quarto R API parity from this figure.





3. Post-build details






NoteOpen: promotion, end hooks, version and optional publication











%%{init: {"htmlLabels": false}}%%
flowchart TB
  classDef default fill:#f0f4f7,stroke:#637b89,color:#153b32
  linkStyle default stroke:#26343f,color:#26343f
  A["[R] Restore renderer config;<br/>stage and validate cache artifacts;<br/>restore native artifacts"]
  B{"Output build?"}
  C{"Analysis and promotion enabled?"}
  P["[R] Promote safe output/docs to<br/>explicitly configured final roots"]
  J{"Publication enabled?"}
  V["[R] Keep successful local release;<br/>close managed recovery boundary"]
  S["[R] Export configured local CAS<br/>destinations, if selected"]
  K["[R] Enabled Git commit / push"]
  D["[R] Run configured end hooks"]
  E{"Output build?"}
  F["[R] Transition to next<br/>development version"]
  G["[R] Restore captured managed<br/>state; retain cache results;<br/>no VERSION publication"]
  A --> B
  B -->|"Yes"| C
  C -->|"Yes"| P --> J
  C -->|"No: including empty analysis"| J
  J -->|"Yes"| V --> S --> K --> D
  J -->|"No"| D
  B -->|"Preview: skip promotion/publication"| D
  D --> E
  E -->|"Yes: immediately after end hooks"| F
  E -->|"Preview: no version transition"| G
  classDef target fill:#fff3d8,stroke:#8a5b00,color:#342600
  class A,P,V,S,K,D,F,G target




Figure 4: Released post-build order with bounded publication/recovery behavior.





The end-hook/next-dev adjacency is approved. The released implementation places enabled CAS export and Git commit/push before end hooks and the next-dev bump. Before publication it records the successful local release and gives up the managed recovery snapshot. Publication or later end-hook failure preserves that local release and skips the bump; partial external effects are not undone. Without publication, end-hook failure still uses bounded managed recovery. Preview runs end hooks, then restores captured managed state without a version transition. These are bounded managed-path guarantees, not whole-project or remote atomicity.
Promotion is output-only and conditional on selected analysis and enabled promotion. Explicit empty analysis preserves existing upload inputs instead; configured publication may still use them. Metadata means existing project/version operations, not finished attempt/release identifiers or complete provenance. The implemented storage path is configured local CAS export; Git commit/push and network checks are opt-in, not consequences of merely having a Git repository.
An analysis failure does not enter the success-only post-clear/promotion/end-hook/version path. This page does not introduce an always/finally-hook policy.

title: Build lifecycle
text:
Released settings







Choice
Meaning




settings.output-clear-stage
none, pre or post; default none.


pre
Clear immediately before selected analysis, after hooks and preparation. Production only.


post
Clear immediately after successful analysis, before restoration, promotion or finalization. Production only.


Precedence
Explicit CLI choice → merged YAML → legacy clear-stage environment fallback → default.


Legacy compatibility
The existing PROJR_CLEAR_OUTPUT fallback and never/no-clear spelling remain supported; canonical no-clear is none.



Preview never clears final outputs. Ordinary generated-output clearing defaults to none; document-output replacement has its own controlled finalization rules.

title: Build lifecycle
text:
Failure and recovery boundaries
The local recovery figure describes the bounded captured-state rule. The separate publication figure adds the released local-publication boundary; it is not a whole-project or remote rollback guarantee.






%%{init: {"htmlLabels": false}}%%
flowchart TB
  classDef default fill:#f0f4f7,stroke:#637b89,color:#153b32
  linkStyle default stroke:#26343f,color:#26343f
  A["[R] Preflight or managed local<br/>step fails; also covers end<br/>hooks when publication is off"]
  B{"Recovery capture exists?"}
  N["Stop: controlled build writes have<br/>not started"]
  C["Restore captured managed set"]
  D{"Restoration succeeds?"}
  E["Report local failure; permitted<br/>cache residue may remain"]
  F["Report primary and restoration<br/>errors; retain recovery data when<br/>available"]
  A --> B
  B -->|"No"| N
  B -->|"Yes"| C --> D
  D -->|"Yes"| E
  D -->|"No"| F
  classDef existing fill:#e5f2ed,stroke:#146859,color:#153b32
  class A,B,N,C,D,E,F existing




Figure 5: Existing local failure boundary: recovery covers only captured state.











%%{init: {"htmlLabels": false}}%%
flowchart TB
  classDef default fill:#f0f4f7,stroke:#637b89,color:#153b32
  linkStyle default stroke:#26343f,color:#26343f
  G["[R] Local success; keep release<br/>version; close managed recovery"]
  H["[R] Enabled CAS export,<br/>then enabled Git commit / push"]
  J["[R] End hooks"]
  K["[R] Next-development bump"]
  I["[R] Publication/end-hook failure:<br/>preserve local release; skip bump;<br/>partial external effects remain"]
  G --> H
  H -->|"Success"| J -->|"Success"| K
  H -->|"Failure"| I
  J -->|"Failure"| I
  classDef target fill:#fff3d8,stroke:#8a5b00,color:#342600
  class G,H,J,K,I target




Figure 6: Released publication boundary: preserve local release; do not undo external effects.





The captured managed set is not a whole-project or filesystem snapshot. Cache results are deliberately retained. Arbitrary external script effects, concurrent writers, crashes and partial storage/Git effects are outside a transactional rollback guarantee. A preview restores its captured managed state on success and failure; this does not make it a security sandbox.
Durable attempt/release records, complete input/code/config/dependency provenance and safe analysis-free publication retries remain unfinished. Do not automatically rerun analysis or claim publication was undone after an external failure.

title: Build lifecycle
text:
Evidence and version boundary

Released source 768da1bf includes reviewed lifecycle PR159, path defaults PR160, R-data PR161, embedding PR162 and combined acceptance PR163.
Actual-main full acceptance passed Rust/event-order/recovery regressions, API docs, real renderer-policy and combined analysis/archive witnesses. Exact-tag delivery passed native binaries and installers on Linux and Windows.
Delivery evidence, behavior and compatibility state source, public-byte/install verification and retained limits. No direct R/IDE parity or M2 completion is implied.

title: Build lifecycle
text:
Maintaining this figure
Contributor requirement: lifecycle changes must update this page’s diagrams, status legend and evidence/version references in the same PR. This includes settings precedence, hook/clearing order, context/version capture, output promotion and publication/failure boundaries. Link actual event-order and recovery tests; do not turn a target marker into a released marker merely because a branch compiles.
Keep the three-stage overview small. Put new detail in the relevant folded stage instead of expanding one unreadable graph. Render the site, exercise diagram export and verify the page links remotely; do not require local Quarto/R/Docker builds.

title: Build lifecycle
section: Failure followed by a smaller build
text:
Failure followed by a smaller build
The controlled order above is unchanged. Remote acceptance now couples the failure branch to a subsequent successful Git build: real HTML and PDF are rendered before a later document fails, previous final/native state is recovered, then a smaller selection is published and its committed bytes are checked. Retained failed scratch stays in cache; it must not enter the later commit. Earlier final docs are preserved on failure and replaced only on successful docs finalization. This is bounded recovery evidence, not a new M2 record or sealing boundary, and does not change the installed preview.2 binary.
The storage design constraints reserve optional future per-directory DVC delegation. Its restore/build/store integration points and error boundaries are still undecided; no DVC step is added to the current lifecycle diagrams. Ordinary native use remains independent of DVC.
The real local-bare-upstream Git tests also check the existing publication-failure branch: a rejected push keeps the successful local release and skips the next-dev bump, while an analysis failure restores managed state without a release commit. This verifies the current boundary without changing lifecycle order, adding a seal or deciding durable attempt/publication records.
Inventory transition tests exercise explicit CAS calls independently of this lifecycle. They do not add automatic pre-analysis input or final-output provenance capture, choose sealing points or complete the unfinished build-record work.

title: Build lifecycle
section: Source CSV inventory: additional capture points
text:
Source CSV inventory: additional capture points
Source change newer than installed preview.2. Released diagrams above retain their status. Production with output_run enabled adds these points without changing clear/analysis adjacency; preview skips CSV capture.






%%{init: {"htmlLabels": false}}%%
flowchart TB
  A["Validate existing CSV history"] --> B["Start hooks and preparation"]
  B --> C["Capture raw / opted-in cache<br/>Save pre snapshot in selected cache when present"]
  C --> D["Existing pre-clear / analysis / post-clear"]
  D --> E["Restore renderer and native state<br/>Promote selected output/docs"]
  E --> F["Capture output/docs<br/>Replace CSV: pre + post + history"]
  F --> G["Existing optional publication<br/>End hooks then next-dev"]




Figure 7: Current source: production CSV capture within managed recovery.





CSV replacement remains inside managed local recovery. Publication failure preserves local release CSV; no remote rollback is implied. Later end-hook changes are outside inventory, so these records are not sealing.
Configured remote restore is a separate explicit operation, not an automatic stage in the build lifecycle above. It selects a source, stages a complete download and then invokes guarded merge/clear installation.

title: Build lifecycle
text:
Configured ordinary publication candidate
Current source (newer than installed preview.2) publishes ordinary local archive/latest targets, then the bounded GitHub latest/archive publication path, before selected CAS export, Git publication, end hooks and next-dev bump. Configuration/planned names are checked and GitHub routing is frozen before hooks. Each provider stages every selected CSV snapshot before its first remote mutation; GitHub preparation additionally checks the remote catalog and shared metadata. This is not a transaction across providers. Failure preserves the local release and skips later stages, without rolling back already published destinations. Preview skips publication. Released diagrams above retain their version meaning.
~{mermaid} %%| label: fig-lifecycle-ordinary-publication %%| fig-cap: “Current-source candidate: ordinary local and bounded GitHub publication.” %%| fig-alt: “Validate configuration and planned names and freeze GitHub routing before hooks. After local success and CSV capture, keep the local release, stage local targets and publish local data then metadata. Prepare all GitHub ZIPs and validate their remote catalog, upload data then metadata, then continue CAS, Git, end hooks and next development version. Failure preserves the release and reports partial effects.” flowchart TB A[“Validate planned namespaces / freeze routing”] –> B[“Existing analysis / promotion / CSV”] B –> C[“Keep local release”] C –> D[“Stage all selected local CSV bytes”] D –> E[“Local archive/latest data, then metadata”] E –> H[“Validate catalog; prepare all GitHub ZIPs”] H –> I[“GitHub latest/archive replacements, then metadata ZIPs”] I –> F[“Selected CAS, Git, end hooks, next-dev”] D –>|Failure| G[“Preserve release; skip later stages”] E –>|Failure| G H –>|Failure| G I –>|Failure| G ~
The ordinary-local publication stage also supports explicit none comparison: source filenames are uploaded blindly according to the documented strategy interaction, after all-target staging and before CAS/Git. This does not change the staged lifecycle diagram or the release-preserving failure boundary.
Ordinary-local latest publication can use the default manifest comparison. History eligibility is resolved from the already captured metadata and project CSV; the staged publication position and failure boundary remain unchanged.
The ordinary-local publication stage now finalises archive or latest targets. Archive comparison eligibility is frozen during all-target preparation; old versions remain untouched and new versions are complete snapshots. Publication ordering and the release-preserving failure branch are unchanged.
The ordinary-publication overlay now stages configured GitHub latest/archive ZIPs after ordinary local finalisation and before CAS/Git. Routing freezes before hooks; all GitHub ZIPs prepare before uploads, data before metadata. External failure retains the local release and skips bump; there is no transaction across providers.
Existing canonical GitHub data is downloaded and merged during preparation. Full uploads precede removal of obsolete empty variants and shared metadata. Replacement DELETE/POST failures report partial or uncertain state; they do not roll back remote assets or the successful local release.
No-inspection GitHub strategies select their merge/purge actions during that same preparation phase. Nonempty purge changes the prepared replacement ZIP; it does not add an early remote deletion phase or change the release-preserving boundary.

title: proj path get
text:
Resolve a project resource independently of your current working directory.
proj path get --label <LABEL> [--target final|safe] [--format auto|absolute|relative] [--relative-to BASE] [--project <PATH>] [PART ...]


Ordinary labels must be declared in the active configuration with a nonempty path. ASCII case is ignored. Undeclared labels and suffixes are errors: declaring raw-data does not declare raw or raw-data-extra. Relative paths resolve against the captured project root; explicit external directories are allowed. Queries do not create directories. Safe lookup is the default and resolves generated output into the versioned cache. Use --target final for the configured released destination.



--project PATH selects that exact existing directory, including a folder without configuration or VERSION. It overrides both ancestor discovery and an inherited run root. Invalid directories fail with a nonzero exit status.
The CLI captures an absolute root as PROJ_PROJECT_ROOT for the invocation and its child processes. A nested proj path get uses that root even after a script changes cwd. An invalid inherited root fails rather than falling back silently. Direct Rust build_project(root, ...) calls also pass their supplied root to children. See the discovery rules below for the recognized root markers.
This establishes CLI child-query behavior, not direct Quarto/RStudio parity or changes to the existing R frontend. Renderer configuration, execution cwd, resource links and output placement remain separate concerns. Path queries do not write ignore files or create the resolved target directories.



Without --project or an inherited run root, discovery walks upward from cwd and selects the first recognized directory. It does not search downward for projects. Recognized markers are VERSION, README.md, _quarto.yml, _proj.yml, legacy _projr.yml, Git/SVN metadata, a DESCRIPTION containing Package:, an RStudio .Rproj whose first line starts Version:, and a renv.lock with a Packages map.
pyproject.toml, Project.toml and JuliaProject.toml deliberately extend the projr marker set for Python/Julia. requirements.txt and Manifest.toml alone are not root markers. Standalone VERSION and README markers are retained, so a nested directory with one is the nearer project; explicit selection overrides it.
Marker recognition does not change shallow default script enumeration or prove that the corresponding language runner/frontend is implemented. Legacy config content handling is a separate compatibility change from recognizing its root.
If no recognized marker exists, discovery selects cwd. Discovery success does not mean a build is configured: the current product contract requires active root configuration and explicit used-directory mappings. Validation changes enforcing that newer contract are separate from this root-discovery slice.



--target safe maps declared output/docs-class labels to <selected-cache>/projr/v<active-version>/<exact-declared-label>. One explicit safe: true cache wins; otherwise eligible exact label cache wins, then the first eligible cache in merged declaration order. safe: false excludes a candidate. The chosen label is captured for child queries. A release version has no dev suffix; dev cache keys use a hyphen, such as v1.2.3-4. Other roles retain their configured targets.
--target final addresses the explicitly configured destination, including an absolute external directory. The CLI defaults to safe; production promotion is a separate build step. Path queries do not promote anything.
Optional parts extend the selected role, for example:
proj path get --label output --target safe figures result.png
Queries do not create directories. Unknown labels, missing cache/version for safe lookup, absolute/drive-qualified parts and parent traversal fail clearly. Explicit directory mappings stay mandatory; output-model does not imply an output alias. Path representation and native execution cwd remain separate policies.



--format auto returns a caller-cwd-relative filesystem path in ordinary execution and an absolute target in an explicitly known managed render child. It never infers render context from a .qmd filename, project marker or cwd. absolute and relative override auto. Explicit --relative-to cwd|project|document|/absolute/base requires relative format; document requires an individually known render document. Project renders without a single document reject that base. A custom base must be absolute.
Strict relative conversion fails across roots/drives. Auto ordinary execution falls back to absolute when no relative path exists; the absolute target stays identical. The CLI defaults to safe targets and auto representation. Merged settings.path-representation may select auto/absolute/relative; an explicit --format overrides it. The default is frozen with managed child context, while relative paths are expressed against each query caller’s current cwd. Getters create no directories.
Renderer descriptors are private per-command snapshots created only when launching Quarto/rmarkdown/Bookdown, alongside unchanged root/profile/version/mapping inputs. Ordinary scripts and dependency probes keep ordinary context. Existing R helpers do not consume this descriptor; direct IDE rendering does not gain automatic parity. Absolute results are filesystem targets, not literal Markdown/LaTeX URL rewrites.



proj path get --label output-r-data --target final
proj path get --label output-r-data result.rda
The first returns project/data even without YAML; the second derives a safe target from the selected declared cache and active version. Neither creates directories nor activates cleanup, recovery, promotion or publication of package data. Explicitly declare directories.output-r-data: {} to activate ordinary output management. Legacy _projr data declarations normalize before merging. Its final destination cannot be redirected. There is no special preservation policy: configured pre/post clearing applies normally; preview never promotes.
Built-in project lookup returns the selected root. No Python, Julia or inst role is introduced; use ordinary output mappings or proj path get –label project inst for a root-relative fragment.

title: proj build
text:
The build pipeline script execution engine for the project.
This command evaluates what files need to be run based on configuration layout parameters (build.scripts in _proj.yml) or filesystem auto-discovery. It sorts them according to strict engine precedence rules, modifies format-specific configuration templates when necessary, and executes each script inside its own independent, isolated subprocess.



--major, --minor, --patch: Specifies the version bump strategy for a production build.
--profile: An optional profile to configure execution context.
--description: An optional description string for the build commit. If omitted during a production build that involves git commits, the CLI will interactively prompt for a one-line description when running inside a valid terminal session.





Pre-flight Dependency Checks: Before modifying files or triggering git snapshots, the build engine statically resolves targets to identify dependencies. Depending on the matched scripts (such as .Rmd, .qmd, or .py) and configuration files, it asserts the availability of Rscript (verifying required R namespaces like rmarkdown or bookdown), quarto, or python executable commands. Any missing R packages can be resolved automatically via the PROJR_AUTO_INSTALL environment variable, or through an interactive terminal prompt.
Production Build Restrictions: Checks if branch rules (only_branches, not_branches) or upstream synchronicity (not_behind) are violated during a production build run.
Remote Export Pipeline: During the post-build phase, conditionally exports resolved local target outputs into a deduplicated Content-Addressable Storage (CAS) vault as defined via build.dest targets in remotes.local.
System Git Provider Abstracted: Git mutations safely resolve through a strictly encapsulated host System Git adapter, securely avoiding hanging inputs and ensuring older systems correctly push mutations.
Mutual Exclusion Checking: Before executing, proj build checks for project-level configurations (_quarto.yml and _bookdown.yml). If both exist and the build targets include Quarto or RMarkdown documents, it throws an error to prevent conflicting rendering.
Explicit Execution (Path A):

Define exact scripts, exclusions (starting with !), or sub-directory globs in _proj.yml under build.scripts.
Can rewrite _quarto.yml or _bookdown.yml configuration if specific subset documents are requested.
Maintains order relative to Python and R scripts, while correctly clustering and executing project documents together.

Fallback Execution (Path B):

If no build.scripts is provided, the engine auto-discovers build targets.
Will execute a Quarto project if _quarto.yml exists, or a Bookdown project if _bookdown.yml exists.
Otherwise, it falls back to a shallow workspace sweep and runs .qmd, .Rmd, .R, and .py files in that strict order.





Every resolved file or project rendering task runs inside its own completely independent subprocess, isolated via environment profiles (PROJR_PROFILE) and correct working directory assignments (current_dir), preventing memory leaks and state pollution across execution runs.



proj build-dev
Development runs execute the existing script selection with development Git settings disabled. The CLI does not create or update VERSION, update ignore files, clear released output or previous caches, promote rendered documents into docs, or export to configured local archives. These rules apply on success and failure, even when production configuration enables cleanup, commits or export.
Scripts should explicitly write preview artefacts into their declared cache or staging locations. A subprocess is not a filesystem sandbox: scripts, hooks and renderers can still write where their own code/configuration directs them. Renderer configuration rewriting and script working-directory behavior retain their existing semantics. This change does not introduce automatic output redirection, recursive discovery or a new project-root policy.



build.scripts: [] selects no analysis scripts. Hooks still run, and production builds can version and export existing artefacts as an upload-only workflow. Analysis cleanup, renderer setup and document promotion are skipped so those existing artefacts are preserved. The CLI does not discover scripts instead.
For previews, an absent dev.scripts inherits build.scripts; dev.scripts: [] overrides it with no analysis. Hooks still run, but previews never publish.



Builds require root-level _proj.yml, legacy _projr.yml, or an explicitly activated _projr-<profile>.yml. Inactive profiles and _projr-local.yml alone do not qualify. Both base filenames together are an error. Unsupported control fields fail before build writes; arbitrary parameters and metadata maps are allowed. Configuration errors include their causes on stderr and return failure.
This validation is separate from project discovery. A root marker or cwd fallback does not make an unconfigured project buildable. Explicit directory enforcement, per-run environment isolation and complete managed-state failure restoration remain under development; see the behavior contract and pinned legacy audit.
Explicit script/hook include patterns must match at least one file. Use an empty list (scripts: []) when intentionally selecting no analysis; unmatched configured includes return an error instead of a successful no-op.
Current source reports directory-enumeration and entry-inspection errors instead of treating a failed fallback scan as an empty selection. Errors name whether fallback discovery or managed-state capture failed and retain the OS cause. The sweep stays shallow, alphabetically ordered within each language, and skips linked entries; hidden and Git-ignored regular scripts remain eligible. This diagnostic correction is newer than preview.2, whose permission failure may appear later as a bare OS error.
Current source also validates every script/hook exclusion pattern before hooks, analysis, clearing or controlled build writes. A malformed pattern such as ![[ fails with a nonzero structured error instead of silently running excluded code. This includes exclusion-only lists and post/both hook selections. Valid exclusions retain include order and first-match deduplication; an exclusion need not match a file. This correction is newer than the published preview.2 binary, which can silently ignore malformed exclusions. Check exclusion syntax before using that installed preview; the source fix does not update it automatically.
Native execution policy (supersedes earlier unconditional root-cwd wording): build and build-dev default to --execution-dir native. Plain scripts/hooks inherit the invocation cwd, not each source file’s parent; R source() normally inherits its caller cwd. Individual Rmd rendering leaves knit_root_dir unset and Quarto receives no execution-dir override, preserving native document/project settings. --execution-dir project explicitly requests captured-root execution for scripts/hooks, Quarto and individual Rmd. Project render drivers run from the selected project root to select the project, independently of chunk cwd. Project-wide Bookdown root override is currently rejected early because its render_site entrypoint does not expose the individual knit-root argument. Captured project/profile/version and logical path identity do not change with execution cwd. No existing R helper bridge or literal Markdown resource rewriting is implied.



Individual Quarto HTML and R Markdown HTML default to embedding resources when unspecified. An explicit format option of embed-resources: false (Quarto) or self_contained: false (R Markdown) is respected. Quarto project defaults use native effective-format inspection, including profiles, directory and included metadata. Only formats leaving both embed-resources and legacy self-contained unspecified receive temporary header settings; original source bytes are restored exactly. Changing a prepared source/input set before rendering is rejected. Other project input types need explicit embedding settings. embed-sources controls source attachment and is unrelated to resource embedding.
Source documents keep their original paths and bytes. Literal Markdown/LaTeX references retain native meaning. Linked output may still depend on its source tree; nonembedded relocation is not supported by this change. Existing restrictions on inherited metadata for individual rendering remain in force. Bookdown site rendering retains its native resource policy and has no new fallback here.
See Quarto HTML embedding and R Markdown render options.
Project embedding preparation keeps native format choices and their order, even when a non-HTML format is the default. Original permissions and external hard-link bytes are preserved. Changing inherited profile/directory/included metadata after preparation is rejected; use literal metadata-files paths. External metadata is read for validation and is not rewritten. Arbitrary external script effects remain outside managed recovery.



Managed renderer failure restores the previous released documents and original native artifacts before a later build can commit. A successful smaller document selection publishes that selection; it replaces the previous final docs tree. Unselected earlier native documents stay unchanged. Failed renderer scratch is retained under the declared versioned cache for inspection, separate from final documents. Cache is disposable and should remain ignored by Git.
The remote acceptance driver tests real individual and project Quarto HTML/PDF renders, a deliberate later-document failure, then a smaller successful local Git build. It compares committed report bytes with both final and cached files, checks the entire commit for failed report artifacts, and preserves retained failed scratch. This adds acceptance coverage to the existing lifecycle, not a new retry identity or transaction guarantee. It does not update installed preview.2 or complete M2 provenance.



Git commits and pushes are separate opt-in actions. A push uses the current branch’s configured upstream, including a differently named remote branch; it must not silently target main. Disabling push still allows a local build commit. The real-repository tests verify both settings against a temporary bare upstream and compare the committed and published CSV bytes.
If Git rejects a push after local analysis and commit succeed, the command fails and reports that the local release is preserved. Its files, local release commit and release VERSION remain available; the next-development bump is skipped. An analysis failure instead restores the previous managed state and creates no release commit. Neither outcome implies a remote transaction or a durable publication record. Do not automatically rerun analysis to retry a failed upload.
No-op commit behavior is tested at the Git provider boundary: unchanged files produce no extra commit, while a real change does. A normal production CLI build advances VERSION and therefore need not be a no-op.



Current source adds root manifest.csv after successful output-enabled production builds. Open it in a text editor/spreadsheet to inspect directory labels, relative filenames, release versions and MD5 values, including earlier versions. Git/remotes are optional; preview leaves production history unchanged. See configuration and limits. This is newer than preview.2; verification evidence is recorded in the compatibility log and PR175.

title: Command exit status
text:
Successful CLI commands return exit status zero. Reported operation failures return a nonzero status and a diagnostic on stderr, including configuration/path queries, version reads/writes, ignore updates and initialization. Argument parsing errors also return nonzero.
For example, a malformed _proj.yml makes proj yml read --project demo fail, so a shell or frontend can stop instead of treating the diagnostic as success. Failed Git staging, commits and GitHub creation propagate as initialization errors; a failed remote inspection does not proceed to GitHub creation.
This defines success versus failure, not stable error codes, a JSON result schema or a capability protocol. Diagnostics remain human-readable text. Commands may perform work before failing; a nonzero status is not a rollback guarantee.


proj build-dev --project demo --non-interactive
--non-interactive disables the CLI’s own prompts and automatic R-package installation, including when PROJR_AUTO_INSTALL=true. Missing dependencies produce an error. Script, hook and renderer runners and controlled R dependency probes receive closed stdin. The mode is inherited by managed children as PROJ_NON_INTERACTIVE=true.
Initialization still performs requested operations using its existing defaults. This flag does not choose project markers, change configuration precedence or define a structured result protocol. Third-party code remains responsible for its own behavior after receiving EOF.

title: Storage and release catalogue design
text: Status: confirmed design constraints, recorded on 21 October 2026. The optional integration and future catalogue described here are not implemented by this note.

title: Storage and release catalogue design
text:
Standalone ordinary use
proj must work with its own native backend without installing DVC. DVC must not become the mandatory manifest engine or a dependency of ordinary proj use. Existing interpreter and renderer requirements still apply to selected analyses.

title: Storage and release catalogue design
text:
Optional DVC-backed directories
Future integration may let users opt individual directories into DVC backing. Only users selecting that integration need DVC. proj should automatically delegate the appropriate operations at the agreed lifecycle points.
proj retains its logical directory labels/roles and path abstraction regardless of backend. Integration must preserve label resolution so analysis code does not depend on DVC-specific physical paths.
DVC remains authoritative for its own tracking and cache state. proj references the corresponding versions rather than maintaining a second authoritative copy of DVC’s data/cache inventory. Projects should be able to mix native and DVC-backed directories. Missing DVC, unavailable data and delegation failures need explicit handling; proj must not silently install DVC.
The directory configuration, supported restore/build/store operations, exact hook timing and failure/recovery boundaries still need design. This note does not adopt old command recipes or decide a provider contract.

title: Storage and release catalogue design
text:
A curated release catalogue
The intended release catalogue is a curated, linear history on the main branch, presented as a readable changelog. A general catalogue of every run on every branch is not the product goal. This direction does not change current build or Git branch policies, or remove the need to report failed attempts honestly.
Attempt/release identity, allocation, sealing and how failures relate to this catalogue remain open. Temporary legacy CSV is approved below. Durable recording architecture, remote-only discovery, retention and Git-tracking policy remain open; this note does not claim M2 completion.
See the behavior contract, current lifecycle and compatibility log for implemented behavior and limits.

title: Storage and release catalogue design
text:
Compatible CSV inventory
Status: source implementation newer than installed preview.2; release pins are unchanged. The user approved temporary projr-compatible CSV while broader recording design continues. This supersedes deferring every manifest implementation.
The root manifest.csv contains quoted string columns in this order: label,fn,version,hash. The filename is relative to its declared directory with slash separators, version includes v, and hash is the lowercase MD5 of file bytes. An empty or absent declared directory has one row with blank filename and hash. MD5 provides legacy comparison compatibility, not authenticity or security.
Production captures hash-enabled raw/cache directories before analysis, after start hooks and preparation. Cache capture excludes its framework-owned projr subtree. After successful output promotion it captures hash-enabled output/docs, then writes those snapshots followed by prior history. Exact duplicate rows are omitted; different versions retain records. With no eligible cache the pre-state stays in memory; otherwise it is also saved at <selected-cache>/projr/<release-version>/manifest.csv. No mapping is invented. Explicit empty analysis can inventory existing artifacts without claiming analysis ran.
Existing history must have the four columns in order and valid rows; corruption fails before hooks instead of being discarded. New CSV writes use guarded same-directory replacement, preserving hard-link aliases. Failure before publication restores root CSV bytes/presence with managed state. Publication failure retains the successful local release and CSV. Cache residue may remain. Previews do not produce production records.
This is an inventory at two lifecycle points, not sealing, environment capture, immutable attempt identity, concurrent snapshot or complete provenance. End hooks run later and may change artifacts. The codec is isolated from build capture for later replacement. CSV has no dependency on CAS. The existing plural .projr/manifests.csv CAS index and remote JSON/objects remain separate, unchanged.

Remote layout direction
projr separates provider configuration from latest/archive layouts. Local providers use path[/label] and path[/label]/v<version>. Store planning includes inspection, cues and sync strategies; restore selects available label versions and copies into final paths. Compatibility includes more than copying a manifest.
Working interpretation: retain ordinary latest/archive and add CAS as a third remote structure, with versioned snapshots and content-addressed objects. CAS can provide archive storage without becoming the manifest format. Current Rust runtime still accepts only local CAS remotes; latest/archive providers, full store/restore policy and CSV-driven queries are not implemented by this slice. Retention, garbage collection and discovery remain open. No DVC dependency.
Pinned reference: manifest, hashing, build capture, defaults, layouts, store, restore.
Existing opt-in Git commit behavior still stages eligible project files, including root CSV unless ignored. This adds no automatic Git requirement or ignore rule. All regular files, including dotfiles, are inventoried; exact R enumeration parity beyond the stated schema/capture comparison remains unverified.

Configuration, defaults, aliases and precedence
R destinations are nested at build.local.<title> or build.github.<title>. The source-selection helpers contain defects noted below; not every accepted shape has demonstrated end-to-end behaviour. Destination storage, source getters, restore selection.



Key or entrypoint
Parsed/defaulted/consumed behaviour
Rust status




Title
Named mapping key. Local helper describes title as descriptive; GitHub title becomes release tag. Internal title helper can derive it from content; public wrappers require the title argument. GitHub wrapper replaces spaces with hyphens.
Configured restore uses named references/inline definitions and GitHub tag space/@version normalization; local title remains descriptive.

Validates allowed labels; send helper treats null/false as none, true as automatic output/raw/docs, vector as selected labels. Boolean helper support and strict validation are not fully consistent. Cache is not in automatic selection.

Restore resolves per-label sources and shared destination definitions. Complete configured store plans remain missing.

title: Projr remote compatibility inventory
text:
Store, inspection and metadata
Production/output builds only enter send; previews skip it. GitHub releases can be prepared/created before analysis when configured. Destination parameters and YAML are resolved per title, then labels are processed in content order. Source files for a send come from the project’s current-version manifest, not an unqualified directory listing. The last label also triggers changelog writing. Preparation, send, planner.








Policy
Implemented operation
Required Rust fixture




upload-all
Add every current source-manifest file; no removal of destination-only names. Existing destinations can be marked untrusted.
Existing extra file retained; source overwrite and empty-label cases.


upload-missing
Add names absent remotely; retain existing remote bytes, including changed same-name content.
Same-name different bytes retained; missing names added.


sync-diff
Add missing/changed files, remove remote-only files; compare via chosen inspection.
Add/change/delete transitions and no-change cue.


sync-purge
Clear/recreate destination content then upload full selected set when plan says needed.
Disposable fixture only; never user dataset destructive tests.


inspect:file
Enumerate/hash remote bytes with legacy MD5, compare to project evidence.
Detect actual byte corruption and ignore mtime/size equivalence.


inspect:manifest
Compare recorded rows/version trust. If unavailable/untrusted, planner may fall back to file hashes.
Matching/missing/stale/corrupt metadata and trust markers.


inspect:none
No comparison evidence; default upload-all and untrusted existing-state handling.
Never label unchecked remote bytes verified.


cue
always or change-driven materialisation/version updates; no trust or no prior destination can force creation.
Unchanged inputs under both cues; empty result snapshots.


Exclusions
Cache inventory excludes projr subtree. File listing includes dotfiles. ZIP helpers accept directory include/exclude and exact filename exclusions; filter implementations differ (pathspec vs regex).
Hidden files, nested names, exclusions and empty-after-exclusion; no regex/pathspec interchange assumption.


Execution
Purge, add, remove, reconcile full/empty, then write manifest, VERSION, and optional changelog.
Failure at each boundary must report partial publication honestly.



Plan execution, ZIP helpers, hashing, listing/path filters.
Local metadata is ordinary manifest.csv, VERSION and CHANGELOG.md at the remote pre-root. GitHub uses manifest.zip, VERSION.zip and CHANGELOG.zip containing those files. VERSION has per-label release entries and optional trailing * indicating untrusted state. These files are distinct from CAS JSON and the plural Rust .projr/manifests.csv index. Metadata.
There is no all-or-nothing remote transaction: local copying/removal can be partial, GitHub whole-asset replacement deletes an old asset before uploading, and metadata is written after content. Metadata-download failures may become empty/unavailable state; some unzip errors are swallowed. Rust should retain its approved safety boundaries, surface errors and never claim rollback of remote side effects. HTTP replacement, GitHub transfer.

title: Projr remote compatibility inventory
text:
Credentials and dependencies
GitHub lower helpers accept explicit token/api_url. Otherwise token lookup is GITHUB_PAT, optional R gh::gh_token, optional gitcreds, GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN. API base is explicit override, GITHUB_API_URL, public API. Enterprise gitcreds lookup strips /api/v3; public lookup uses https://github.com. Requests carry an Authorization header and may be unauthenticated without a token. Repository inference prefers origin then first Git remote, using available gh R helpers or system Git/gert. Explicit Enterprise overrides are not forwarded by every wrapper. Authentication, repo inference, HTTP.
These are source mechanisms, not authorisation to obtain new credentials, change permissions or install dependencies. Rust should use supported existing access, mock HTTP for fixtures, redact secrets and never store tokens in CSV/URLs. Current Rust transport accepts explicit API/token inputs; configured restore uses GITHUB_API_URL and existing GITHUB_PAT/GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN values. Explicit repository selection avoids Git; inference currently uses origin only and checks its host against the API. R gh/gitcreds fallback and first-other-remote inference remain missing. R helper auto-install behaviour is not adopted. Real Git remains an optional installed dependency; GitHub CLI is separate and need not be mandatory for an API implementation. Optional managed Git is not planned by default.

text:
Source defects and documentation-only surfaces
These are source-review findings, not executed reproductions or requirements to copy bugs. Keep claims bounded until fixture evidence exists.

Default source selection passes an inner mapping where the next helper expects the provider mapping; explicit provider selection can call a title-specific helper with a null title. Selection.
GitHub existence checks hard-code label/version names, ignoring some custom path/append-label settings; local archive discovery assumes a label directory. GitHub existence, version paths.
Title send-check reads top-level cue while defaults populate send.cue; the cue setter also writes a different level. Send, defaults.
get/conflict fields are validated but no effective execution consumer was found. wrapper docs mention never/version and OSF, outside actual enums.
GitHub unzip failures can be swallowed, clone restore ignores partial failure, and low-level asset deletion can infer the current repo despite a repo argument. GitHub, HTTP, clone.
Content option sets, wrapper checks and boolean auto-content helpers differ; special code/package labels alone do not prove working end-to-end export.

title: Projr remote compatibility inventory
section: Critical configuration assessment, separate from compatibility
text:
Critical configuration assessment, separate from compatibility
This assessment excludes the agreed temporary CSV choice. Examples use the existing R inline build configuration, not a newly approved Rust schema. Findings are source-backed; unless stated otherwise they are not executed reproductions. Proposed fixes are review candidates, not silent semantic changes.



Rank/type
Example and user impact
Smallest proposed fix




High: ineffective accepted setting
A destination with send: {conflict: skip} passes allowed-value checks, but store execution never reads conflict. get: {strategy: upload-missing, conflict: error} similarly has no restore consumer. Users can believe a non-overwrite policy is enforced. Checks, execution.
Reject ineffective combinations until implemented, or implement and test them explicitly. Do not silently ignore a safety control.


High: colliding-target combination
build.local.shared with content: [raw-a, raw-b], structure: latest, path-append-label: false, send: {inspect: file, strategy: sync-diff} gives both labels one physical directory. File inspection can classify the other label’s files as extras. Custom archive/pre-root paths also assume layouts not uniformly supported. Layout, planner, versions.
Resolve all target identities before mutation and reject collisions; verify supported custom-prefix/append combinations rather than accepting untested layouts.


High: destructive restore ordering
A normal configured restore source plus projr_content_update(clear=TRUE) clears the destination before source resolution/download. A missing release or failed network call can leave data gone. clear defaults FALSE; this is an unsafe opt-in ordering, not an unsafe default. Restore.
Download into private staging, validate, then apply guarded promotion. Preserve current data on lookup/download failure.


Medium: surprising default synchronisation
build.local.shared: {path: backup, structure: latest, content: [output]} defaults to sync-diff, so remote-only files can be removed. A user expecting an additive backup may be surprised. Default archive keeps prior version directories, which narrows the risk. Defaults, planner.
Clearly expose adds/removes and the resolved strategy before applying; require deliberate review before changing defaults. This is a usability/policy concern, not evidence that sync-diff itself is defective.


Medium: profile cannot disable with null
Base build.github.archive selects output; a local/profile build.github.archive: null inherits the base mapping. Removing one active-profile destination also does not remove its base definition. Merge.
Explain merged effective destinations and provide a deliberately designed disabling/empty-selection mechanism. Do not reinterpret null without an approved compatibility change.


Medium: argument precedence surprise
YAML build.local.archive: {content: [raw-a], path: backup} means archive_local=c(‘raw-b’) does not replace that archive definition. always_archive also defers to explicit archive YAML. Dispatch.
Document this as YAML authority and display the resolved content; avoid presenting these arguments as ordinary overrides. Whether arguments should override is a design choice.


Medium: two cue locations
send: {cue: always} is completed and used per label, while title-level send checking and the setter reference top-level cue. This invites inconsistent getter/setter behaviour; nested cue is not simply unused. Send, defaults.
Use one canonical nested location and test the public setter through an actual store plan; treat an alias only through explicit conflict rules.


Medium: provider-dependent identity
build.github.nightly: {id: another-tag, content: [output]} validates an id, but completion resets it to nightly. Local id instead becomes path. Title is cosmetic locally and functional on GitHub. Completion.
Reject or clearly deprecate ignored id values; document title/tag/path meanings. A larger unified identity design is separate.


Medium: source-selection defects
directories.raw-data.source: {github: archive}, as shipped in the template, meets default helper paths that pass the wrong mapping level or an absent title into a title-specific branch. Template, selection.
Fix source selection with explicit/default provider/title fixtures; do not require users to discover accidental nesting workarounds.


Medium: unsupported documentation
send.cue: never and structure: version are mentioned in wrappers but excluded by current enums; old OSF prose outlives implementation. Wrappers, enums.
Correct docs and errors. Implement new values only if separately requested, not to make stale prose true.


Already recorded design
Removing a build destination can remove a historical restore source because definitions and upload selection share the same location.
The user-requested registry proposal is already issue706, design-only. It is not a new discovery here and is not implemented by this audit.


Low: naming preference
dest versus destinations changes readability, not provider or safety behaviour.
Choose during the existing registry discussion; no new alias or migration silently introduced.



Credential lookup also deserves explicit presentation: ambient R gh/gitcreds resolution precedes GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN, and repository inference may choose origin or the first remote. A supplied environment token or repository can therefore differ from a user’s expectation. The smallest safe improvement is clear resolved host/repository diagnostics without secrets, plus tests for explicit overrides; no new credential permissions are implied.

section: Test evidence and bounded implementation sequence
text:
Test evidence and bounded implementation sequence
Test sources were inspected without running R. Fixtures must establish behaviour before fixes are claimed; a source test title alone is not an acceptance result.







Source coverage
What it establishes here

Remaining slices should stay independently testable:

Configured ordinary publication: cue/inspection policies, shared metadata history updates, empty-variant reconciliation and all-destination namespace preflight before mutation. Existing explicit transfer commands are foundations, not evidence that this combined lifecycle already runs.

title: Future R wrapper: CLI installation and CRAN checks
text:
Status: design direction recorded on 2026-10-20, not a shipped wrapper or an accepted CRAN submission. The existing R package remains untouched. This note does not settle the complete frontend protocol or claim renderer parity.


The future wrapper is intended to contain R code that calls a separately installed proj CLI. Its DESCRIPTION should declare that CLI in SystemRequirements. It should discover a compatible executable and give an actionable missing/incompatible-CLI error. A user-invoked installer on the user’s own machine is distinct from automatic downloads during CRAN installation, checks or examples. Do not assume CRAN servers already provide proj.
CRAN source-package policy permits downloads of precompiled software only as a last resort with CRAN-team agreement. A separate executable is not an automatic exemption. Review Writing R Extensions: portability when implementing the package, including external software availability and portable invocation. This work has neither requested nor obtained CRAN agreement; no outreach is authorized here.










Environment
Required behavior




CRAN, CLI absent
Always run meaningful R-only validation, argument construction, missing-CLI diagnostics and mocked protocol/response tests. Skip only genuine executable integration tests, explicitly because the CLI is unavailable.


CRAN, compatible CLI available

Our integration CI
Install an exact pinned CLI release, verify its checksum and compatible version, and run real end-to-end tests. Missing CLI or failed installation is a failure, never a silent skip.



Mocked responses check the wrapper contract; they do not prove the CLI or renderer works. Our mandatory integration job supplies that evidence. Examples and vignettes must also handle optional executable availability honestly instead of requiring an undeclared download. title: Preview feature status
text:
Preview feature status
The published development release is 0.4.0-preview.2. The verified WSL user-local command also reports that version. See release evidence for the exact source and checks.
This is an early Rust CLI for disposable analysis projects. A development preview does not mean the complete roadmap is finished. Use independent backups and sample data while evaluating it. The existing projr R package and thesis remain unchanged.



Area
Available Rust behavior
Verification and limits




Project selection
Explicit root; nearest recognized ancestor; markerless cwd fallback; shallow default script discovery.
Cross-platform fixtures cover markers, nested invocation and explicit override. Root recognition includes Python/Julia markers; that does not imply Julia execution or a wrapper.


Configuration and init
Active root YAML required; legacy alias/ambiguity rule; profile precedence; explicitly declared resource directories; local-only directory initialization.
Cross-platform configuration/error-preservation fixtures. Old no-config roadmap assumptions were superseded.


Execution context
Ordered explicit scripts/hooks; native cwd with explicit project-root override; supported Quarto/R Markdown root controls; unsafe/unknown layouts fail early.
Real Python/R/rendering acceptance and cross-platform fixtures passed. Direct R API/IDE parity remains unproved.


Automation
Opt-in protocol-v1 JSON, capability version, typed queries, noninteractive command worker, nonzero failures; child logs on stderr.
Cross-platform machine tests. Static coarse error codes; no invented attempt/release record on success.


Preview preservation
The released CLI restores captured managed state after successful/failed previews. Cache results remain.
Included through the reviewed recovery dependency; final integrated tests and actual released-binary checks passed. Generated-output path queries use the safe cache by default; arbitrary writes are not isolated.


Production safety groundwork
Path guards, bounded local failure recovery, optional checked Git publication and verified CAS bytes.
Focused fixtures and reviews; incomplete release identity/provenance/retry model. This page is not an invitation to run on valuable production data.


Binary delivery
Development prerelease 0.4.0-preview.2 supplies versioned Linux/Windows x86-64 assets with mandatory checksums.
Exact-tag workflow, uploaded/public asset hashes and both native binary smokes passed. WSL user-local installation and tiny success/failure Python previews passed. Other platforms are not supplied.



Still unfinished: direct projr/quarto R API/RStudio parity, existing R helper integration, automatic isolation of every script write, durable attempt/release identifiers, complete input/code/config/dependency provenance, multi-writer/crash atomicity and analysis-free publication retry. Capture/recovery cannot undo arbitrary external script effects or guarantee concurrent readers never observe temporary changes. User/third-party logs are not automatically secret-redacted.
M1 is delivered as the useful local CLI preview in 0.4.0-preview.2. It requires active root configuration; initialization is optional. Explicit file-based R/Python/report steps, captured context, inspectable cached results and honest structured failures work without Git credentials. Supported previews preserve recorded final/archive/version state on success and failure. Runtime path guards and preflight remain essential; arbitrary child code is not sandboxed.
General command/argv forms, stronger process confinement and broader maintenance audits remain follow-ups. M2 records/provenance/retry and later frontend work are not completed by M1. See delivery boundaries, behavior and the compatibility log for supported details and remaining gaps.

text:

directories:

build:

proj --project . --non-interactive build-dev
The step-by-step example supplies the script, a tiny dataset, and the result to check. It uses Python’s standard library.
