title: Configuration _proj.yml
text:
The _proj.yml file dictates the structural map of your project. It configures the foundational paths and mapping logic used by the CLI.


Custom directory labels are strictly validated against a set of foundational prefixes: - cache - raw - output - docs
These prefixes are case-insensitive. Any label defined in the configuration must begin with one of these approved identifiers.



Ordinary declared directories need a nonempty path. The fixed R-package role output-r-data: {} is the exception: its final destination is project/data. Runtime does not insert other missing cache/raw/output/docs mappings or synthesize subpaths for undeclared labels. Canonical data/data-* labels are rejected; see the R-package data section for the legacy per-layer data alias. For example, declaring raw-data: {path: _raw_data} makes raw-data available; it does not create an undeclared raw or raw-data-extra resource. ASCII case is ignored and case-only duplicate labels are rejected.
proj --project . --non-interactive init directories creates a missing _proj.yml once with explicit raw-data: _raw_data, cache: _tmp, and output: _output paths. It preserves existing base/profile files, creates only declared resource directories, and does not invoke Git/GitHub or add an R code directory. The preset omits build.scripts, preserving shallow discovery; it never serializes an accidental empty analysis list. To render documents, declare a docs mapping too.
Production state and project-render staging require a declared cache directory. Framework version/staging children are derived inside that declared cache; this is distinct from inventing undeclared resource labels. Storage content labels must be declared and relative storage paths use the captured project root.



Each cache-class directory may include boolean safe. One explicit safe: true selects that cache; otherwise an eligible exact cache label wins, then the first eligible cache in merged declaration order. safe: false excludes a candidate. Profile/local overrides retain existing declaration positions. For example:
directories:
  cache:
    path: _tmp
  cache-analysis:
    path: _analysis_cache
    safe: true
This selects _analysis_cache for explicit safe logical output lookup. Multiple true selections, non-boolean values (including null), selection flags on non-cache roles, and all declared cache candidates excluded are validation errors. Each layer’s explicit values are checked before merging; null cannot inherit a previous boolean. Cache-free queries and operations that do not consume a cache remain valid. The chosen safe cache is frozen in child run context. Cleanup, safe lookup and renderer staging consume that same selected mapping; no literal cache label is required when another eligible cache is selected.



The system performs strict validation on _proj.yml: - If a defined directory label uses an unsupported prefix layout, a validation error string will be returned and execution will fail. - All references must resolve correctly; otherwise, the CLI will output an error detailing the structurally invalid labels or malformed content.



The _proj.yml file supports a top-level config block for project-wide settings:

config.git.engine: The Git execution engine to use. Can be auto (default) or system. This determines how the CLI interfaces with Git capabilities natively.
config.git.use_proj_cred_helper: Defaults to false: use existing native Git authentication. Explicit true permits an existing single-line GITHUB_PAT, GH_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN for standard HTTPS github.com remotes through a temporary host-scoped helper. There is no automatic token discovery or GitHub CLI call during builds. Tokens are environment data, never argv or shell source; persistent auth settings are unchanged.




The _proj.yml file supports a top-level parameters block for arbitrary nested parameter evaluation. This allows you to define custom metadata and deeply queried values throughout your execution environment.
The configuration engine also supports several aliases for this block: parameter, params, and param. However, multiple alias conflicts within the same configuration file are structurally rejected during validation to prevent mapping confusion.



The _proj.yml file supports a top-level remotes block, which currently supports a local mapping of standalone storage vaults.

local: A mapping where keys represent remote titles and values configure the vault:

path: The physical absolute or relative path to the remote storage directory.
structure: Specifies the storage structure algorithm. Must be cas (Content-Addressable Storage).
content: An array of string tags (matching foundational prefixes or defined directories) specifying which project output directories to sync into the remote upon build completion.
inspect: manifest validates JSON, logical paths/digests and manifest filename/content identity; file additionally hashes every referenced object and compares actual bytes. Manifest-only inspection does not verify object bytes.





The _proj.yml file can also contain a build block to configure the behavior of the proj build and proj build-dev execution engine. The build block supports the following sub-keys:

dest: An optional list of remote target strings. These targets must be mapped to explicit configurations within the remotes.local block. During post-build execution, resolved content directories matching these tags are piped to the CAS engine for deduplicated storage synchronization.
scripts: An optional list of explicit script paths or glob patterns to execute during the build pipeline.

Globbing patterns are supported.
Prefix a pattern with ! to exclude matching files from execution.
Current source rejects malformed inclusion or exclusion syntax before execution, including hook patterns. The exclusion correction is newer than preview.2; see the build reference.
When provided, this selects scripts instead of automatic discovery. Document targets may be grouped for rendering, so mixed script and document targets are not guaranteed to run in the exact listed order.

hooks: An optional map of lifecycle hook scripts to execute.

pre: Scripts executed before the actual build phase.
post: Scripts executed after analysis/promotion, before VERSION and publication.
both: Scripts executed during both pre and post phases.

profile: An optional environment profile identifier. When set, the system injects the PROJR_PROFILE environment variable into the isolated subprocess for all executed scripts and project rendering commands. This can be overridden at runtime via the --profile CLI flag.
git: An optional Git integration configuration. This can be a boolean toggle or an object mapping out detailed toggles:

commit: Defaults to false, including inside an existing Git repository. Explicit true requires initially clean Git state and commits once after successful local build; an unchanged staged index is a successful no-op.
push: Defaults to false. Explicit true publishes HEAD to the current branch’s configured upstream remote/reference. Missing upstream or custom push-only routing fails before build writes; origin/main is never invented.

restrictions: Configuration block to enforce Git checks specifically during production builds:

only_branches: A list of allowed branch names. Production builds will abort if the current branch is not in this list.
not_branches: A list of restricted branch names. Production builds will abort if the current branch is in this list.
not_behind: Omitted/false performs no fetch. Explicit true fetches the current configured upstream and compares its state. If enabled, production builds will verify that the local branch has an upstream tracking remote and is not behind it, aborting if the local branch needs to pull upstream changes.

clear_output: An optional string controlling workspace clearing routines for output directories. Can be set to "pre", "post", or "never". If omitted, defaults to evaluating the PROJR_CLEAR_OUTPUT environment variable.




You can define a dev block to completely override specific configurations during development builds (proj build-dev).

scripts: A list of script paths or globs. During development builds, this array entirely overrides build.scripts. An explicitly empty array ([]) selects no analysis scripts. An absent dev.scripts inherits build.scripts. Hooks can still run.
hooks: A mapping identical to build.hooks. When specified, these completely replace build.hooks during a development build.
old_dev_remove: Retained configuration field. The current preview protections skip CLI cleanup of prior caches during development builds, even when this is true. Scripts and hooks still control their own writes.





PROJR_AUTO_INSTALL: During the proj build pre-flight checks, if required R packages (like bookdown or rmarkdown) are missing, this environment variable controls remediation. If set to true, packages are automatically installed. If absent or set to false, the tool defaults to an interactive terminal prompt (if available) or fails hard.




build declares actions; settings controls how they run. Parameters are analysis inputs, not execution controls. This is an intentional extension beyond projr.
settings:
  output-clear-stage: none
  execution-directory: native
  path-representation: auto
Use none to preserve other existing final files, pre to clear immediately before analysis, or post to clear immediately after successful analysis and before output promotion/finalization. Preview never clears released outputs. Pre-hooks run before pre-clear; end hooks run after finalization immediately before the next-dev bump. The command’s explicit –output-clear-stage overrides merged settings; those override legacy build.clear_output, then PROJR_CLEAR_OUTPUT, then the new none default. Legacy never is accepted in the legacy field/environment. The canonical settings key accepts only none/pre/post, with invalid values/null rejected before merge or mutation. execution-directory accepts native/project; explicit --execution-dir wins over merged settings, then native is the fallback. Native scripts inherit launch cwd; native document execution remains renderer-defined. path-representation accepts auto/absolute/relative; explicit path-query --format wins over merged settings, then auto is the fallback. Auto is caller-relative ordinarily and absolute in a known managed renderer. Both settings reject null, booleans and unknown values in each active file before merging. Managed child queries retain the captured representation policy even if scripts change configuration, profiles or cwd. Safe is the default path target; final must be explicitly requested. Docs output handling and the R-data built-in remain separately modeled features.



The built-in output-r-data lookup has fixed final destination project/data, even without YAML. Querying never activates build management or creates directories. Safe lookup needs the selected declared cache and active version.
To opt into ordinary output clearing and success-only promotion:
directories:
  cache:
    path: _tmp
  output-r-data:
    ignore: []
An empty output-r-data mapping also activates the role, with ordinary default ignore rules. Explicit ignore: [] includes package data in Git and R builds. The path may be omitted; if present it must resolve to project/data. Redirection is forbidden. settings.output-clear-stage applies normally: pre/post clears old package data; the default none preserves other final files. Preview never promotes final data.
Legacy _projr.yml and active _projr-*.yml layers accept data as an alias and normalize it before merging, including legacy remote content labels. Defining both aliases in one layer is an error. Canonical _proj.yml requires output-r-data. Generic data-* labels are unsupported; use raw-* inputs or ordinary output-* mappings.



CAS ingestion records the current recursive file paths and content hashes for the explicitly selected directory. The transition fixture compares exact inventories and stored bytes after a same-size/same-modified-time edit, an addition, a rename and a deletion. Earlier snapshots remain inspectable across those later ingestions. A renamed file appears under its new path in the current snapshot; this does not create a rename-event format.
This verifies existing archive machinery only. It does not automatically record all build inputs, code, configuration or dependencies, select a future build record format, or decide content-only identity and retention policy. Complete M2 provenance remains unfinished.



Current source adds directory boolean hash. It defaults to true for declared raw/output/docs labels and false for cache labels. Set hash: false to omit a directory, or hash: true to include a cache. Each active layer must use a boolean; null, numbers and strings fail validation before hooks.
directories:
  raw-data: {path: inputs}
  cache: {path: _tmp, hash: false}
  output: {path: results}
A successful output-enabled production build writes root manifest.csv, without requiring Git or a remote. Preview and build.output_run: false leave that CSV alone. See the inventory notes. This is newer than installed preview.2. See the compatibility log and PR175 for verification evidence.



The current source’s explicit remote restore command reads the existing projr directories.LABEL.source and build.local/build.github definitions. See the remote command reference for lookup precedence, limits and safety. This does not enable automatic ordinary uploads in build; normal build validation still rejects unsupported publication fields. The future top-level registry proposal remains separate. _proj.yml and legacy _projr.yml discovery/conflict rules remain unchanged.
Configured restore uses the shared profile selection order: explicit profile, PROJR_PROFILE, QUARTO_PROFILE, then build.profile, with earlier profiles winning and local overrides last. Machine failures preserve installation/recovery details on stderr, including retained backup paths; stdout stays a structured failure. Legacy data CSV rows and remote data namespaces are read without rewriting history; ambiguous canonical/legacy namespaces fail before installation. One optional VERSION trust marker is accepted; it is not a byte-verification claim.
Review precision: VERSION.zip requires exactly the canonical VERSION member spelling, including on case-insensitive filesystems. Metadata transfer staging also closes explicitly and reports cleanup failure paths.



build.local.TITLE accepts selected latest destinations with explicit send.inspect:file. See the remote command reference for the complete example and tested/pending control matrix. content:false/null disables a destination, true selects declared non-cache roles, and a list retains its explicit label order. Each selected role must have CSV hash capture enabled. The existing if-change/sync-diff defaults remain; omitted inspect does not silently change the projr manifest default to file.
Archive, manifest/none inspection, path-append-label:false, title-level cue and nonempty get/conflict controls are not executable in this bounded slice. Selected unsupported policy fails before hooks. Registry706 remains design-only.
For configured ordinary local latest publication, explicit send.inspect: none selects blind source-file planning and defaults send.strategy to upload-all. Explicit upload-missing/sync-diff then overwrite source filenames while retaining remote extras; sync-purge only purges when the source is nonempty. See the remote control matrix before choosing these combinations. Omitted inspection retains the projr manifest default, using matching recorded history or falling back to physical file comparison.
Configured ordinary build.local publication now follows the archive default when structure is omitted; latest remains explicit. The existing manifest inspection and sync-diff/if-change defaults apply. See archive publication for historical reuse, complete snapshots and unsupported append-label:false.
The first build.github upload subset requires explicit send.inspect: none and upload-all (the none default), with archive as the existing structure default. Other decision combinations and existing current-version data fail explicitly. See the remote CLI page for credentials, metadata bounds and partial failure.

Auto is caller-relative ordinarily and absolute in a known managed renderer. Both settings reject null, booleans and unknown values in each active file before merging. Managed child queries retain the captured representation policy even if scripts change configuration, profiles or cwd. Safe is the default path target; final must be explicitly requested. Docs output handling and the R-data built-in remain separately modeled features.

title: Configuration _proj.yml
text:
The built-in output-r-data lookup has fixed final destination project/data, even without YAML. Querying never activates build management or creates directories. Safe lookup needs the selected declared cache and active version.
To opt into ordinary output clearing and success-only promotion:
directories:
  cache:
    path: _tmp
  output-r-data:
    ignore: []
An empty output-r-data mapping also activates the role, with ordinary default ignore rules. Explicit ignore: [] includes package data in Git and R builds. The path may be omitted; if present it must resolve to project/data. Redirection is forbidden. settings.output-clear-stage applies normally: pre/post clears old package data; the default none preserves other final files. Preview never promotes final data.
Legacy _projr.yml and active _projr-*.yml layers accept data as an alias and normalize it before merging, including legacy remote content labels. Defining both aliases in one layer is an error. Canonical _proj.yml requires output-r-data. Generic data-* labels are unsupported; use raw-* inputs or ordinary output-* mappings.

title: Configuration _proj.yml
text:
CAS ingestion records the current recursive file paths and content hashes for the explicitly selected directory. The transition fixture compares exact inventories and stored bytes after a same-size/same-modified-time edit, an addition, a rename and a deletion. Earlier snapshots remain inspectable across those later ingestions. A renamed file appears under its new path in the current snapshot; this does not create a rename-event format.
This verifies existing archive machinery only. It does not automatically record all build inputs, code, configuration or dependencies, select a future build record format, or decide content-only identity and retention policy. Complete M2 provenance remains unfinished.

title: Configuration _proj.yml
Configuration _proj.yml
text:
The current source’s explicit remote restore command reads the existing projr directories.LABEL.source and build.local/build.github definitions. See the remote command reference for lookup precedence, limits and safety. This does not enable automatic ordinary uploads in build; normal build validation still rejects unsupported publication fields. The future top-level registry proposal remains separate. _proj.yml and legacy _projr.yml discovery/conflict rules remain unchanged.
Configured restore uses the shared profile selection order: explicit profile, PROJR_PROFILE, QUARTO_PROFILE, then build.profile, with earlier profiles winning and local overrides last. Machine failures preserve installation/recovery details on stderr, including retained backup paths; stdout stays a structured failure. Legacy data CSV rows and remote data namespaces are read without rewriting history; ambiguous canonical/legacy namespaces fail before installation. One optional VERSION trust marker is accepted; it is not a byte-verification claim.
Review precision: VERSION.zip requires exactly the canonical VERSION member spelling, including on case-insensitive filesystems. Metadata transfer staging also closes explicitly and reports cleanup failure paths.

title: Configuration _proj.yml
text:
build.local.TITLE accepts selected latest destinations with explicit send.inspect:file. See the remote command reference for the complete example and tested/pending control matrix. content:false/null disables a destination, true selects declared non-cache roles, and a list retains its explicit label order. Each selected role must have CSV hash capture enabled. The existing if-change/sync-diff defaults remain; omitted inspect does not silently change the projr manifest default to file.
Archive, manifest/none inspection, path-append-label:false, title-level cue and nonempty get/conflict controls are not executable in this bounded slice. Selected unsupported policy fails before hooks. Registry706 remains design-only.
For configured ordinary local latest publication, explicit send.inspect: none selects blind source-file planning and defaults send.strategy to upload-all. Explicit upload-missing/sync-diff then overwrite source filenames while retaining remote extras; sync-purge only purges when the source is nonempty. See the remote control matrix before choosing these combinations. Omitted inspection retains the projr manifest default, using matching recorded history or falling back to physical file comparison.
Configured ordinary build.local publication now follows the archive default when structure is omitted; latest remains explicit. The existing manifest inspection and sync-diff/if-change defaults apply. See archive publication for historical reuse, complete snapshots and unsupported append-label:false.
The first build.github upload subset requires explicit send.inspect: none and upload-all (the none default), with archive as the existing structure default. Other decision combinations and existing current-version data fail explicitly. See the remote CLI page for credentials, metadata bounds and partial failure.

title: Build execution flow
text:
This describes the current Rust implementation, not a complete correctness or reproducibility guarantee. The behavior contract records approved semantics and the compatibility log records evidence and gaps.


Capture the project root, resolve a private per-run environment without changing the parent process, require active root configuration, and merge base/profile/local settings. Validate fields, explicit directory paths, targets, hooks and destructive destinations. Explicit empty scripts select no analysis. Otherwise explicit globs or shallow root discovery select inputs; project rendering may use its own input discovery. Explicit Python-only selection does not activate an unused Quarto/Bookdown project marker.
Read VERSION with DESCRIPTION/default fallbacks. Check selected interpreters and configured Git restrictions before controlled project writes. Existing preflight can still invoke Git/network checks or R package remediation; these are known limitations, not a clean-environment guarantee.



Before authoritative writes, capture exact bytes, permissions and presence/absence for the managed set documented in the compatibility log. This includes VERSION, ignore/configuration files, existing root regular files, selected in-project inputs, declared output/docs trees and planned individual rendering artifacts. External declared output/docs directories are allowed. Linked managed trees are rejected. Backups stream into private OS temporary storage outside disposable project cache. Backup creation failure prevents authoritative project writes.
One local error/panic boundary covers ignore synchronization, requested pre-cleanup, pre/both hooks, script/document execution, renderer configuration, promotion and post/both hooks. Required output promotion errors propagate. Renderer configuration is restored exactly, retaining comments and originally absent keys. Candidate version changes stay in memory; VERSION is written only after those stages succeed. No pre-build Git commit is created.
On local failure, restore the captured managed set, including originally absent files/directories. Attempt all restorations; retain recovery backups and report both the primary and restoration errors when recovery fails. This does not undo arbitrary script effects outside the captured set or provide a filesystem sandbox, power-loss atomicity or protection against concurrent filesystem replacement.



Storage export and Git publication start after successful local completion. Export actual declared content before requested clear_output: post cleanup. Create one configured final Git commit, then push when enabled. A publication or later cleanup failure reports that local analysis succeeded and retains its release/version; external publication is not rolled back.
Git upstream/authentication policy, stable attempt/release records and an analysis-free publication retry command remain unfinished. Push uses the captured current-branch upstream; custom push-only routing remains unsupported and fails before authoritative writes. Native authentication is the default.



Previews skip production version changes, cleanup, commits and exports. They run selected hooks/analysis and restore captured managed state after success and failure, while cache output remains. Scripts still choose preview output locations; this is not automatic output redirection or an OS sandbox. Script/hook subprocesses start with the captured invocation cwd by default. Only an explicit project execution mode passes Quarto an execution-directory override; individual R Markdown receives a non-null knit_root_dir only in project mode. Direct R/IDE parity remains unfinished and is not established by these CLI controls. The existing R package remains untouched.
Native execution policy (supersedes earlier unconditional root-cwd wording): build and build-dev default to --execution-dir native. Plain scripts/hooks inherit the invocation cwd, not each source file’s parent; R source() normally inherits its caller cwd. Individual Rmd rendering leaves knit_root_dir unset and Quarto receives no execution-dir override, preserving native document/project settings. --execution-dir project explicitly requests captured-root execution for scripts/hooks, Quarto and individual Rmd. Project render drivers run from the selected project root to select the project, independently of chunk cwd. Project-wide Bookdown root override is currently rejected early because its render_site entrypoint does not expose the individual knit-root argument. Captured project/profile/version and logical path identity do not change with execution cwd. No existing R helper bridge or literal Markdown resource rewriting is implied.

Capability
What it means for you




Choose the project

Detect command failures
Errors produce a nonzero exit status, so an automated run can stop.

Production builds can export configured outputs to local content-addressed storage, which avoids storing identical content repeatedly.

title: What works
section: Known limits of the published preview
text:
Known limits of the published preview

A preview is not a filesystem sandbox. Scripts and hooks control their writes; automatic redirection of every renderer’s output is not provided.
Matching results and paths across CLI runs, RStudio and GUI rendering has not been proved.
Complete compatibility with every projr workflow has not been established.
Mixed script and document targets do not have a complete sequential-order guarantee.
This preview supplies only Linux and Windows x86-64 binaries; macOS and ARM delivery are unavailable.
Production recovery is bounded. It does not undo arbitrary script writes or partial external publication effects.

The existing R package is unchanged. A Rust library is available in this repository, but new R, Python and Julia frontend integrations are separate work.

Included in preview.2

title: Preview release delivery
text:
The reviewed pipeline prepares a draft prerelease for an existing vX.Y.Z-preview.N tag whose version exactly matches Cargo.toml. It does not bump versions, push commits, publish an APT repository, sign credentials or publish the draft automatically. No new release is implied by this documentation.
Remote locked tests/builds produce Linux x86-64 and Windows x86-64 binaries. Linux uses Ubuntu 22.04 (glibc 2.35 or newer); the initial user-local WSL installation target is Ubuntu 24.04 x86-64. macOS/ARM delivery is not verified or supplied by this pipeline. Each asset is named proj_<version>_<os>_<arch>[.exe], with matching version.txt and checksums.txt. Exact-tag help/version/protocol smokes and actual installer tests must pass before assets enter the draft. Checksums detect corruption and mismatches; they are not independent signatures or reproducible-build attestations.
Installers default to MiguelRodo/projcli, require version metadata and exactly one matching SHA256 entry, and verify downloaded bytes before replacement. They stage on the installation filesystem and need only an existing user-writable directory. PROJ_RELEASE_VERSION pins a release (with optional v); preview releases should always be pinned because GitHub’s latest URL normally selects stable releases. PROJ_INSTALL_DIR selects an existing absolute user directory without changing PATH or system settings. Existing older releases lacking the new metadata fail closed instead of installing an unverified fallback binary.
Before publication: reconcile reviewed supported behavior and limits, update the Cargo/Cargo.lock preview version in a reviewed change, verify required checks, then create the exact reviewed tag. Inspect the resulting draft assets/version/ checksums and retain disposable-project warnings. Publish only after those checks. For WSL, download the pinned binary/manifest, verify SHA256, preserve any existing user-local binary, install into the chosen user-local directory and smoke help, version, capabilities and a disposable configured preview. No local compilation, sudo, persistent authentication change or R package modification is needed.
Known limits include bounded captured-state recovery, arbitrary external script effects, incomplete direct R/IDE parity, incomplete attempt/release records and analysis-free publication retry. This is a development preview, not M2 completion.

title: projcli 0.4.0-preview.2
text:
projcli 0.4.0-preview.2
This development preview adds the CLI analysis workflow described below. The exact tagged source commit is recorded in source-commit.txt; checksums.txt verifies both platform downloads. These notes are prepared before publication.
Run selected R/Python analysis steps from one project configuration, inspect temporary results, and keep the project identity stable when code changes folders. Generated-output paths default to the selected versioned cache. Declared final outputs are promoted only after successful production analysis; previews do not promote or publish. Output cleanup defaults to keeping other final output files, with explicit pre/post cleanup options. Document-output replacement follows its separate documented rules.
Scripts use the launch folder and document tools retain their native working-folder settings, unless a project-folder override is explicitly requested. The R-package output-r-data role has a fixed final project/data destination; querying it never opts that folder into cleanup or promotion. Declare it explicitly to activate ordinary output management. Supported legacy declarations normalize before merging.
Individual Quarto/R Markdown HTML and modeled Quarto projects default to embedding resources only when unspecified. Explicit and inherited false values remain respected. Bookdown’s site renderer is unchanged and has no new embedding fallback. Linked-output portability and literal Markdown/LaTeX resource rewriting are not provided. Existing R helpers/packages are unchanged; direct R/IDE parity is not claimed.
Remote acceptance covers manual configuration and fresh local directory initialization, ordered real Python/R/report steps, a computed CSV and embedded report, deliberate structured failures, ordinary generated-output/archive preservation under none and local archive publication without Git credentials. Prior document outputs are preserved on preview/failure and replaced by successful finalization. Final files and archived object bytes must match the computed witnesses; manifest/ index release and next-development versions are checked, with corruption probes. The reviewed release source must pass the full integrated gate, including all 26 renderer-policy cases, eight combined workflow cases and seven archive corruption probes per successful production case.

Use sample data or an independently backed-up disposable project. Recovery is bounded and does not isolate arbitrary external script effects, concurrent writers or power loss. Complete provenance, durable attempt/release records, analysis-free publication retry and M2 remain unfinished.

title: Machine interface
text:
Use proj --machine <command> for automation. Human command output remains the default. proj capabilities (also with --machine) reports protocol/capability versions and supported command families without loading a project.
Protocol version 1 writes one JSON object and a newline to stdout. Both success and failure include protocol_version, cli_version, ok, result, and error. result is null on failure; error is null on success. Failures exit nonzero. Broken output pipes cannot receive a complete object and also exit nonzero.
proj --machine capabilities
proj --machine --project . path get --label output
proj --machine --project . version get
proj --machine --project . yml read
proj --machine --project . build-dev
Successful queries return { "path": "..." }, { "version": { "major": 1, "minor": 2, "patch": 3, "dev": 0 }, "text": "v1.2.3" }, or { "validated": true }. Configuration queries validate without returning raw configuration or parameter values. Other existing command families reuse the ordinary CLI in a noninteractive subprocess and return { "completed": true } only when that command succeeds. Unsupported command arguments fail; capability flags explicitly report absent preview isolation, attempt/release records and direct R/IDE parity.
Stable error codes are invalid_arguments, project_selection_failed, query_failed, command_failed, and worker_unavailable. Messages are static; raw config, environment values, command arguments and chained domain errors are not copied into protocol errors. This transport reuses existing anyhow domain handling tracked by issue87; it does not promise a finer domain-error taxonomy. With --machine, help/version display requests return capability negotiation.
All command progress and child stdout/stderr go to stderr, streamed directly without accumulating logs in memory. Machine mode closes child stdin and enables noninteractive policy. Child logs are user/third-party output and are not a secret redaction service; avoid printing credentials in scripts. No environment/config dump is included in the machine result. Callers must keep stdout and stderr separate.
A failed publication can follow successful local analysis. command_failed is not a rollback or retry instruction: inspect local state/diagnostics before retrying. No analysis-free publication retry or successful release record is invented here.


Current source adds remote versions to capability negotiation, independently of the installed preview. Its successful result is an object containing versions, an array ordered newest-first for archive layouts. Each entry contains version (a leading-v numeric string), path (the actual physical directory), empty and present booleans, and metadata_untrusted (the latest VERSION asterisk boolean, or null for archives). An empty result is versions: [].
Present means a real directory exists, not that its contents match metadata. Neither false nor null metadata_untrusted proves integrity. Failed queries use query_failed without returning the raw path or filesystem error. See the command reference for layout and missing-target semantics.
The mutating remote download command follows the existing noninteractive worker route, returning completed: true on success and command_failed on failure. See its command reference for the explicit destination and bounded recovery contract; a failed post-install cleanup is not an instruction to repeat blindly.
Current source adds remote store –dry-run as a read-only plan query. Its result contains plan with source, destination, strategy, uploads, overwrites, removals, same_bytes and applied=false. Normal remote store uses the existing worker route and returns completed:true only after success. This file-policy command does not publish remote metadata or load configured source/destination policy.

title: projr compatibility and change log
text:
The behavior contract owns current product decisions. This log records comparison evidence, implementation differences and gaps. Update it in every focused PR; do not infer runtime parity from similar source or green Rust CI.
Relationship labels are same, different, new, and unverified. Each entry states whether that label concerns documented intent, static source, or executed behavior. No comparative R runtime tests have been run for the entries below. Local R/Docker workloads have not been run.



R baseline: SATVILab/projr at 3ac2959.
Thesis baseline: design at b110da5.
Rust pre-migration baseline: 024589b.

New comparisons must pin source commits and relevant files, record the decision and rationale, link executed tests, and distinguish approved, implemented and unverified behavior. Changing a reference baseline does not silently change the product contract.




Relationship: unverified runtime parity; same documented intent. The R README and thesis design describe development previews separately from publication. This is evidence of intent, not proof that every R development path is inert.
Decision/rationale: keep CLI-managed release/version/archive changes out of previews so researchers can inspect development results without publishing.
Implemented: PR123, merged 5d145293e596c5797e9620bd3f00978fa6f99411; Dev-gated VERSION writes, cleanup, document promotion, local export and ignore updates in build.rs, env.rs and yml.rs.
Executed evidence: three-platform Rust tests, including test_preview_safety.rs, and installer checks passed on reviewed head 5d3ac227f52b33fd0c32fddd479cb7296c4072a5. A disposable installed-CLI Python fixture reproduced the previous version/output/ignore mutations.
Gaps: cooperating Python scripts only; renderer YAML rewriting, automatic output isolation, repeated runs, same-project concurrency and full production lifecycle behavior were not established. Subprocesses are not a sandbox.





Relationship: new explicit contract; renderer parity unverified. R path.R dynamically discovers a root, while the thesis defines the project workflow.
Decision/rationale: current approved behavior supersedes defects and stale architecture claims. Root/path defaults must agree across projr, quarto::quarto_render() and RStudio QMD Render. Quarto root equals proj root; nested Quarto projects are unsupported. Direct rendering does not imply release lifecycle parity; R Markdown Knit is a separate entrypoint.
Implemented: PR124, merged 635aa9efac0d7a28971236ab78c879b21be5ec31, corrected AGENTS/README/flow guidance and added the behavior contract. This was documentation, not renderer code.
Executed evidence: independent document review and remote Rust CI passed at dbf8d5fd94a87bba32ffc95cd2ee3b47f1e04277.
Gaps: no direct R frontend, Quarto/RStudio GUI or fresh-render-session parity test was performed. No projr production code or thesis text was changed.





Relationship: different root-resolution mechanism; new CLI selection. R path.R calls root discovery from current context. The CLI now captures one absolute root and passes it to each managed child as PROJ_PROJECT_ROOT.
Decision/rationale: explicit selection wins, and path queries must not change projects after cwd changes. This deliberately improves unstable root behavior rather than copying it.
Implemented: PR125, merged f265eb46c91a300fe0aafad3119d998038946a0b; project.rs, ignore.rs, main.rs and build.rs. Direct library builds configure each child command instead of mutating the caller’s process-global root.
Executed evidence: three-platform tests at 779b3010040eeb23f08434478e0812173eb2a723 cover explicit precedence, spaces, invalid roots, changed cwd and overlapping builds in two distinct roots.
Gaps: marker discovery was not changed; R path helpers and direct render entrypoints do not yet consume this captured context. The tests do not promise general environment isolation or same-project concurrent builds.





Relationship: same static read-only configuration intent; runtime R parity unverified. R yml.R reads/merges configuration; this does not establish equivalence of every R public path helper or its cache routing.
Decision/rationale: reading configuration or paths must not update ignore files. Mutating build/init operations request synchronization explicitly, and bad configuration must not replace custom ignores with default rules.
Implemented: PR126, merged cd34c3208f1ed1c3c27571e7ce2828498a4aecdb; yml.rs, build.rs, init.rs/main.rs.
Executed evidence: three-platform tests at cc132f1e1b288c7560ff6b6b06fcac369a475355 snapshot files/directories for CLI queries, exercise direct API reads and production ignore synchronization, and preserve custom ignores on malformed/read-failing config. Permission-denied coverage ran on Linux/macOS.
Gaps: supported aliases, unknown-option handling and effective merged script/hook configuration remained unchanged and incomplete.





Relationship: new CLI transport contract; same failure-reporting intent. R build-engine.R uses R errors; that is not a process exit-code protocol for language wrappers.
Decision/rationale: a printed error must not be returned as successful execution. Failed Git remote inspection must not proceed to GitHub creation.
Implemented: PR127, merged 8e955b32bc1f611d38a8931d489de2bdfc50d5c7; main.rs routes operation failures to nonzero status and init.rs propagates previously swallowed external failures.
Executed evidence: three-platform tests at a741b5f9de63dcb96ca527607105e5547be1da7c cover failing queries/version/init/ ignores, missing executables, child failure and successful queries. Local fake Git/GitHub commands on Linux/macOS made no network requests.
Gaps: structured error/capability protocols and clean/idempotent Git-init coverage remained open; failure status is not rollback or R-runtime parity.





Relationship: new CLI mode. The R baseline’s build-engine.R calls dependency helpers; no equivalent explicit CLI flag/parity is claimed.
Decision/rationale: machine invocations must not need the CLI’s prompts or automatic package installation. Controlled child stdin must actually be closed.
Implemented: PR128, merged f7ff7e92451a3174d6cb9c5fd60151621e66bd04 after independent review at 5dedee7da69cbe52837993e86bc4837c4c3342a1; adds the flag, inherited mode, runner stdin closure and controlled R-probe stdin closure.
Executed evidence: three-platform tests and installer checks passed at that head; fake-R EOF/no-install tests ran on Linux/macOS and Python runner-stdin coverage ran on all three platforms.
Gaps: no actual R startup/renderer execution comparison; initialization retains existing requested-operation defaults and third-party code can ignore EOF. This does not establish general subprocess isolation.





Relationship: same absent-dev fallback; different explicit-empty guarantee. R yml-scripts.R falls back when dev scripts are absent. Empty-list behavior also passes through validation and renderer selection, so a reliable R upload-only no-analysis contract has not been demonstrated.
Decision/rationale: explicit [] selects no analysis, preserving hooks and production upload/export; absence still falls back. It must not discover or render unrequested files. Cleanup/promotion must preserve upload inputs.
Implementation status: PR129 removes the Dev-empty error and derives one analysis-selection guard for renderer setup/cleanup/promotion. tests/test_empty_scripts.rs checks hooks, existing output/docs bytes, actual production archive bytes and preview nonpublication.
Executed evidence: three-platform Rust tests and installer checks passed at f4b3739554dc548911019c450ca1e90a196d33d2; independent review inspected those logs and cleared that code head. The documentation-only final head 999b730fd2cc23215e4a07a1231d7d6fa3543966 passed all nine checks in runs 39486028024/39486028097 and independent review. Merged as 5617a6daed1f4743a9b2609694a2f84ad4c902eb; post-merge test, installer and site runs 39486858711/39486858532/39486858701 passed.
Gaps: YAML null-as-absence and malformed-list validation were inspected in source, not newly exercised by this policy slice. No R runtime empty-list parity test or real renderer execution is claimed.
Confirmed but separate runtime gaps: retain projr markers (including README/ VERSION), accept legacy _projr.yml with a both-base-files error, and use local > profiles > base with earlier profiles first. The R precedence evidence is yml.R. These approvals are recorded in the behavior contract; this change does not implement aliases, marker expansion or merged script/hook context.




The actual .agents/skills/ponytail/SKILL.md is vendored unchanged from DietrichGebert/ponytail v4.10.0, upstream commit e3ba2aa6f1e6f0bc4d69eb09c9f0d0a93af56156, as installed by PR121. Its pinned upstream bytes and the existing projcli, projr, setupmjr and projects copies all have SHA-256 1316a2f3f95741d2300b116fe0c2d81ce4a9568656ed0a62643f54aaf09957f2. The established setupmjr vendoring contract matches; no duplicate or replacement skill was installed.
The skill prescribes the full-mode simplicity ladder, tracing callers before changing shared behavior, reusing existing code/stdlib/dependencies, and leaving an appropriate runnable check. It supplies no separate executable review script. Applying that guidance is a self-review, separate from independent review and CI.
Completed-chunk review of PR128 at 5dedee7da69cbe52837993e86bc4837c4c3342a1:

Traced the prompt helpers, main description prompt, dependency probes, install branch, script/hooks and project-render runners. Reused the existing EnvGuard, one shared mode predicate and standard-library null stdin; no dependency or custom execution framework was introduced.
Finding/action: the R package probe also needed closed stdin before package detection. That path was corrected and covered by a live-input/fake-R EOF test. Rechecking all controlled status/output paths found no further necessary change.
All three remote Rust suites and installers passed; this self-review remained separate from the independent exact-head review.

Completed-chunk review of PR129’s empty-selection change:

Reused the existing explicit-list resolver and pipeline; no new execution framework, configuration key or dependency was added.
Traced preflight, version, cleanup, hooks, document promotion and publication. Finding: skipping script execution alone could still erase upload-only inputs or require unused renderers. Action: derive one shared analysis-selection guard and apply it before those stages; keep hooks/publication outside that guard.
Retained data-preservation and failure handling. Added runnable integration checks for real archive bytes and absence-versus-empty semantics; those checks passed on all three remote platforms at the code head recorded above. No R runtime parity was inferred.





Relationship: same static projr marker intent; deliberate extensions. projr path.R at 3ac2959 combines VCS, VERSION, README, R-package, RStudio, renv and Quarto criteria. Exact structured-marker patterns were checked in rprojroot root.R at 4d2f450.
Decision/rationale: retain those markers with nearest-wins; remove Rust’s VERSION-first/five-extra-ancestors heuristic. Add pyproject.toml and Julia Project.toml/JuliaProject.toml as requested language extensions. Proj config files also anchor a configured project without VERSION. Requirements/orphan manifests do not create roots. Explicit selection still wins.
Implementation/evidence status: root_from now tests each ancestor once, never child projects. tests/test_root_markers.rs covers retained marker patterns, invalid structured markers, weak/nested markers, deep invocation, explicit override and a configured Python preview with shallow enumeration. At code head a0d459c5b3a31437443832436535b70d34838553, all nine checks passed in runs 39487247962/39487247928. Independent review compared the pinned marker sources and inspected all three platform logs, clearing that head. Symlink normalization was source-inspected, without a new dedicated test. Final evidence-only head 55e5606e7916f78de7dfb03a4bb43b0ae1a87987 passed all nine checks in runs 39487685152/39487685131 and independent review; merged as 41bd7000363f34b1e7e2d7e354971bfe9021e2b1. No R-runtime parity is claimed.
Gaps: required active config, explicit used-directory mappings, early unsupported-setting validation, legacy config-content aliases and full frontend/renderer parity are separate changes. A marker does not claim a Julia runner exists.
Ponytail full-mode review: reused the public root_from entrypoint, existing regex dependency and standard filesystem APIs, replacing the old special-case traversal instead of adding a discovery framework. Traced explicit/inherited precedence and all root callers. Kept discovery read-only and shallow, with runnable positive/negative predicates and workflow coverage; no new dependency.





Relationship: different from prior convenience-default assumptions. The initial Rust/projr-style defaults and historical no-config fixtures are no longer the target behavior. Builds require active root-level configuration and explicit used-directory mappings; init may write familiar defaults into that file, but runtime must not invent missing directories or unknown subpaths.
Decision status: approved. The agreed _proj.yml / legacy _projr.yml names apply; explicitly activated profile files may provide configuration, while inactive profiles alone do not satisfy the requirement. Cwd discovery fallback does not waive build validation. Unknown behavior-affecting settings must fail before mutation.
Failure/publication target: restore pre-build state except permitted cache residue; storage/publication retry must not rerun or mislabel analysis. Existing staging/version/publication behavior does not yet prove that transaction.
Evidence/gaps: earlier CI entries remain accurate historical evidence for their source commits, not acceptance of the superseded no-config/default-path policy. Future fixtures must declare used paths and active configuration. The current core still needs enforcement and failure tests for the new rules.
Authorship boundary: the existing R package is entirely off limits, including root-helper fixes. A later backend port/integration must establish R parity; no such work or runtime comparison is claimed here. Thesis text remains untouched.





Relationship: same projr local > profiles > base precedence, with earlier-listed profiles winning; legacy _projr.yml is accepted alongside canonical _proj.yml as an explicit compatibility decision. Both base files together fail instead of silently merging. Source comparison remains projr yml.R at 3ac2959.
Implemented: shared base selection for merged reads, existing build base inspection, parameters insertion and local-profile cloning. Explicit profile lists replace ambient lists; traversal-like explicit names fail validation. Profile/local files retain their existing _projr- names in this bounded slice.
Evidence: new runnable query/alias/ambiguity/preservation/precedence tests passed on all three platforms at 53463d325c85c538ae0b8a5e792caa6bc997e452. All nine checks in runs 39488461110/39488461213 passed; independent review inspected alias, precedence and duplicate-key logs and cleared that head. Final documentation/instruction head c8b208f9243f828de05977f8e76d6f2074535a9b passed all nine checks in runs 39489639669/39489639654 and independent review; merged as 0fec2735355ee5e9b9ba64d33ecd4796bf396301. Post-merge checks passed. No R runtime tests.
Gaps: one merged build script/hook context, active-configuration requirement, explicit directory mappings and early unsupported-setting validation remain separate work. This does not claim builds yet satisfy those approved rules.
Ponytail full-mode review: traced base filename readers and reused one stdlib path selector; reversed existing deep-merge traversal rather than adding a merger or dependency. Preserved null-as-absence and explicit-empty-list behavior. Checks exercise real query results and preservation on ambiguity.

PR131 failure-path review found that direct YAML-to-JSON deserialization allowed duplicate keys to overwrite earlier values. Restored YAML Value parsing before JSON conversion, preserving duplicate-key rejection at every active layer. Added top-level and nested duplicate-key regressions for both base filenames, profile and local files, including CLI failure before preview state writes. The prior green CI did not cover this malformed-input case; the corrected head above passed the new checks and independent re-review. Ponytail review kept this at the shared file parser rather than guarding individual callers.




Relationship: new/unverified design. The durable CRAN note records the discussed future R-code wrapper around a separately installed CLI, meaningful unconditional R-only/mocked tests, conditional executable integration on CRAN, and mandatory pinned/checksummed CLI integration in our own CI. It cites current policy and pinned Quarto precedent.
No existing R code or tests were changed; no CRAN submission, agreement, preinstalled executable, automatic-download exemption or renderer parity is claimed. Implementation and runtime validation remain future work.
Ponytail full-mode design review: kept one linked design note; reused the repository’s behavior/compatibility/AGENTS pointers. No installer, wrapper, binding, mock framework or external contact was added speculatively.





Relationship: follows projr’s merged-configuration intent and the approved local > earlier profiles > later profiles > base precedence. The prior Rust pipeline validated merged settings but separately reread the base for execution.
Implemented: deserialize and validate one merged value, then select scripts and hooks from it. Explicit empty dev selection remains empty; absence falls back to build settings. Both base filenames use this same execution path. Configuration parsing/validation, target resolution and preflight now precede production environment-ignore writes.
Evidence: runnable Python fixtures check conflicting profiles, legacy base, local dev overrides and hook results, plus invalid merged configuration with a local environment file and missing-target failures leaving ignores/version/cache untouched. Remote CI and independent review pending; no real R/renderer execution is claimed.
Gaps: required active config, explicit mappings, all unsupported-field rejection and transactional rollback remain separate approved work. Environment loading still uses the existing process-global guard; this change makes no new same-process concurrent environment guarantee.
Ponytail full-mode review: removed the second base-only YAML parser and its ignored parse failure instead of adding a second configuration model. Reused existing typed validation and dev fallback rules. Traced validation, selection, hooks and environment-ignore writes; retained explicit error propagation.




The 2026-10-20 static audit records the pinned baseline, reported failure paths, required regressions and correction order. Its findings are not runtime reproductions or completed fixes. Highest managed-state risks remain blockers to production-safety claims; arbitrary external script effects are outside managed rollback. No mechanical edition upgrade or CAS redesign is claimed. This review uses the actual Ponytail full-mode skill to prioritize root causes and data-preservation checks over cosmetic rewriting.




Relationship: deliberate difference from projr convenience defaults, as explicitly approved. Every build requires a base file or activated profile; inactive profile/local files alone do not qualify. Discovery still falls back to cwd independently. Empty analysis is valid with active configuration.
Implemented: build gate before writes; unsupported typed configuration fields fail instead of disappearing in a top-level filter. Build failures include their error causes so unsupported-field diagnostics name the field. Arbitrary parameter and metadata maps remain supported and parameter aliases reach validation.
Evidence: runnable tests cover active/base/legacy/inactive/local/no-config cases, unsupported nested keys, dynamic maps and no pre-build state writes. Remote CI/independent review pending. Explicit directory enforcement is still a separate gap; this does not yet establish transaction/promotion safety.
Ponytail full-mode review: reused Serde’s unknown-field validation and the existing active profile resolver; removed silent filtering from runtime reads. No new parser/schema/dependency. Kept the old public filter helper only for compatibility; runtime no longer uses it.

PR134 merged-context evidence: exact head 29b2bdfb564f3193a0e93eb43096f89f2691653a passed all nine checks in runs 39490264159/39490264169. Independent review inspected the three new regressions across platforms and cleared the bounded change. Merged as eb1204026e8809780fc783f27b0be7edf9b5033e. Preflight itself is not guaranteed read-only; environment/profile-source unification, per-run environment safety, strict directories and transaction/promotion safety remain open. This evidence is batched with the substantive active-configuration change to avoid an extra matrix.
PR135 review found mixed parameter aliases survived per-file parsing as separate keys and then conflicted at typed deserialization. Canonicalize the one accepted alias to parameters in the shared reader before merging. New fixtures cover all 64 base/profile/local alias combinations, earlier-profile precedence and retained nested values; same-file multiple aliases and YAML duplicate keys remain errors. Ponytail full-mode re-review kept the fix at the shared loader, without caller guards or a second merge model. Exact amended CI/re-review remain required.




Relationship: new safety checks, not a blanket ban on external resources. Before production analysis cleanup, reject root/ancestor destinations, staging and resource overlaps, selected-input containment, VCS metadata, label path separators and symlinked managed-write paths. Directory replacement also requires an existing source and disjoint destination before deleting bytes.
Evidence: runnable preservation fixtures cover root, ancestor, staging, raw/output overlaps, traversal labels, Unix symlink parents and low-level self/ancestor/nested/missing-source moves. Remote CI/review pending.
Limits: does not yet provide atomic promotion or complete rollback, protect against concurrent hostile filesystem replacement, undo user-script external effects or establish full CAS integrity. External disjoint paths remain valid.
Ponytail full-mode review: one stdlib identity resolver shared by build and promotion guards; trace all promotion callers, retain explicit errors instead of silently accepting missing source/read errors. No new dependency.

Path-guard Ponytail re-review traced the public cleanup helpers as well as build: direct clear_pre/clear_post now apply the shared destination checks, clear_old rejects symlinked staging parents, and traversal-bearing version components fail before cache deletion. Label separator validation lives in shared typed validation for all modes. Generic destructive move APIs require resolved parents and reject symlink aliases; positive direct-API fixtures canonicalize their temporary roots so macOS system temp aliases do not violate that explicit safety precondition. Added a direct-cleanup preservation fixture. This is not complete transactional restoration or a guarantee against concurrent filesystem replacement.
PR135 final evidence (batched with path guards): code head 3839173366e55cffa946ea0e2afe4757ae48e77d passed all alias/conflict regressions on three platforms and independent re-review. Base-update head abc62f966766915093351c00a6a1724a0d1b69da changed no executable/tests/Cargo code, preserved the published site, passed all ten checks in runs 39492001512/39492001479/39492001493 and focused independent review. Merged as a0909e413915847498e77669a3b669941dbfe3fe. Required active config and unsupported field rejection are implemented; explicit used-directory enforcement and finite control-value validation remain separate gaps.
PR137 independent review found that configured-root checks alone missed derived version/output cache leaves. Validate all actual cleanup bases before the first deletion, including configured-cache and legacy staging paths. Direct dev cleanup is now a true no-op. The same review traced individual document promotion and recursive copying: validate paths before creating directories or renaming files, require actual outputs, reject traversal/aliasing and prevalidate asset moves. The two duplicate individual-renderer helpers now reuse one guarded implementation. Added targeted direct-API regressions; amended remote CI/re-review are required. This does not yet fix build callers discarding promotion errors or provide full restoration/atomicity; those remain the following focused work.
The repaired PR137 guard prevalidates concrete generated-file/asset paths and both legacy/configured cache-derived leaves before VERSION/ignore writes, including dangling links. Individual and project promotion now resolve the configured docs destination rather than a root/docs fallback; Python-only builds do not clear unrelated docs. Unix fake-Quarto/fake-R CLI fixtures exercise the reported linked root/docs sentinel bypass and actual successful external promotion, without a real renderer installation. Direct helper tests remain cross-platform.
Project-render source safety is explicitly conservative: recognized source-like .qmd, .Rmd, .md and .ipynb files or links in managed cleanup trees cause an early error. This can reject generated Markdown there; it is not exact Quarto or Bookdown input discovery. Keep sources and managed destinations separate until a renderer-provided input plan is supported. Quarto’s documented project input types are described in Project Basics.
The prepared literal-root glob fix is included in PR137 because a metacharacter root otherwise hides explicit inputs from the cleanup containment guard. Reuse glob::Pattern::escape for the root prefix only, retaining user include/exclude syntax. Runnable tests verify actual analysis bytes and selected-input preservation under a bracket-containing root. This is the same audited root-cause fix, not an additional discovery policy or dependency. Existing standalone preparation remains preserved and must not later be merged as duplicate work.
Windows CI at 9938173 exposed a skipped explicit failing script. Source review of glob 0.3.3 confirmed that escaping the canonical Windows namespace changes its filesystem prefix. Normalize Disk/UNC namespaces for glob transport only, keep filesystem prefixes literal, escape only directory components and join patterns using native path operations. The captured root is unchanged. Explicit include patterns with no files now fail instead of reporting successful no-op execution. New native/canonical-root execution markers run on every platform; network UNC execution remains unverified.
The same review found generated filenames could overwrite another selected script or hook, DESCRIPTION or environment configuration. Before renderer invocation, compare all concrete output/asset paths against the complete selected-input set and reject authoritative project/environment metadata filenames. Fake-renderer fixtures prove those failures happen before scripts, VERSION or ignore writes. Amended exact-head CI and independent re-review remain required.



Different (approved): runtime directory resolution requires declared nonempty paths and never invents missing labels or suffix subpaths. This supersedes earlier in-memory directory-default behavior, including read-only path queries. Missing configuration can still be queried as an empty inventory; builds require active configuration. Storage content labels must exist, and relative storage locations resolve against the captured root. Selected cleanup and project-render staging require cache; upload-only empty analysis does not require an unused cache mapping. Rendered documentation requires docs. Cache cleanup uses the declared mapping, not a parallel hard-coded _tmp tree.
Same preset / different timing: pinned projr 3ac29595d0e39552495d863661b99ea015d59d3d, R/yml-dir.R:334–345, supplies raw-data: _raw_data, cache: _tmp, output: _output. Rust local-only proj --project . --non-interactive init directories writes those explicit paths once when no base/active profile exists. Existing configuration stays byte-for-byte intact. No scripts field is generated: absence preserves discovery, while an existing explicit empty list stays empty. No Git/GitHub/R setup is invoked. The Rust accepted label-prefix subset still differs from projr’s broader labels; this slice does not claim full schema parity or R frontend changes.
Ponytail full-mode review reused the shared resolver and existing tempfile dependency rather than adding a directory framework. Existing malformed/unreadable config preservation tests remain; new tests cover missing paths, undeclared labels, case collisions, explicit storage references, cache ownership, no-executable local init, preserved base/legacy/profile bytes and actual default-discovered Python output. Remote CI and independent review are pending. Init is not an atomic transaction against filesystem failures or concurrent replacement.
PR137 final eb727912f2f0302d01611cca7b84188d34c34e82 independently cleared; all ten checks passed (runs 39496127892/39496127915/39496127894). Merge 56564b9a4aeeef03ae199b04140b5f3d325b3505 passed post-merge test and installation runs 39496869636/39496869586 and published the site in 39496869590.
Independent PR139 review removed an over-broad production cache prerequisite. Only selected operations that consume cache require its mapping. Explicit empty analysis can export declared existing results without cache/docs mappings. An explicit Python-only selection does not activate a renderer merely because its project marker exists. The custom-cache fixture now executes Python and checks actual custom staging cleanup plus preserved legacy _tmp bytes. Fake-R fixtures declare docs while retaining EOF/no-install assertions. These amendments require fresh remote checks and exact-head re-review.



Same precedence / deliberate error handling difference: inherited OS values win over local, earlier environment profiles, then base assignments. Preserve non-Unicode inherited values rather than treating them as absent. Reject empty, equals-containing or NUL keys and NUL values before calling OS mutation APIs. Read whole files with propagated errors rather than lines().flatten(); required file errors and directory inputs cannot silently bypass validation or loop. Diagnostics include paths/line numbers, never assignment values. Same-file validation finishes before assignments from that file are applied. Ignore writes in explicit activation occur only after validation succeeds.
Ponytail full-mode review traced all load/assignment callers and reused existing configuration-entry presence checks. No parser dependency was added. Prepared CLI checks cover invalid/NUL entries, directory and permission-denied required files, secret-free diagnostics, actual inherited/local/profile/base child values and no analysis invocation on errors. Remote checks/review are pending.
This bounded fix does not make EnvGuard thread-safe: process-global environment mutation remains a known risk until per-run values and profiles reach all child commands and Git/preflight consumers. No credential handling or CAS code changes. ## Prepared managed-state restoration invariant (not yet verified)
The restoration implementation under preparation replaces the legacy middle-only catch and synthesized development-version rollback. Before controlled production mutations, capture exact bytes, permissions and absence for VERSION, ignore files, root configuration/state and existing root regular files; selected in-project inputs; declared output/docs directory trees; and concrete individual renderer output/asset paths. Capture initially absent parent directories too. Declared external output/docs paths are supported. Raw data, Git internals, arbitrary external user-script effects and cache contents are not backed up. Managed trees containing symlinks or unsupported entries are rejected rather than followed.
Backups use existing tempfile and streaming std::fs copies in private OS temporary recovery storage outside disposable project cache. No project mapping is invented, and cache-free upload-only operations remain supported. Recovery sources are copied to temporary restore staging before any current target is removed. Missing recovery bytes leave intact current state alone and are reported as unavailable.
One local failure boundary covers ignore synchronization, cleanup, all pre/both/ post hooks, engine configuration, execution, output promotion and VERSION writing. Promotion errors propagate; renderer configuration is restored byte-for-byte on success and failure. VERSION changes only after hooks/render/promotion succeed. Failures and caught panics restore captured state. All restore entries are attempted; if restoration fails, retain recovery bytes and report both the original failure and restoration failures with the backup path. Substituted links are rejected.
After local success, storage export/Git publication form a separate failure phase: publication failure reports successful local analysis and retains the new local release. Export precedes requested post-output cleanup so archives contain actual build bytes. A failure during this later cleanup is explicitly reported as such; there is no external publication rollback. No pre-build Git snapshot or second post-build commit is needed. Upstream selection/native credentials and publication retry identity remain separate unfinished work.
Prepared checks cover each hook/analysis failure, initially absent VERSION, exact old output/docs bytes and empty directories, renderer execution/missing promotion, exact YAML comments/render lists, restore-failure backup retention with external sentinels, and successful local analysis followed by failed storage publication. These are unrun: no local compilation under memory pressure; remote CI and independent review are still required. No power-loss atomicity, concurrent-writer or global script-side-effect guarantee is claimed. M2 attempt/release records and analysis-free retry commands remain open.
PR141 review corrections: normalize selected-input identities before comparing root containment (including Windows namespace forms); require nonempty supported document artifacts before project promotion; remove prior expected individual artifacts and project staging immediately before rendering. New regressions cover nested scripts/hooks modifying or deleting themselves, empty renderer staging, stale individual artifacts, cache purge during failed analysis, and unavailable recovery bytes without further deletion. These amendments require fresh remote CI and independent review. Project artifact scanning remains a conservative supported-document check, not a complete renderer manifest guarantee.
Further review keeps project promotion conservative: require a freshly created tree containing a nonempty supported document, rather than guessing per-input filenames from incomplete document-only format metadata. Fake PDF rendering tests cover explicit and inherited project formats. Complete expected-output manifests remain unimplemented; individual document format inference is still a separate known limitation. Selected managed script/hook paths reject symlinks along the original path before canonical identity comparison. System recovery temp anchors are canonicalized, including cache-free operations, without weakening user-path symlink rejection.
Bookdown’s framework-controlled <book_filename>_files source/destination are resolved and guarded before writes, with default _main and portable custom stems. text:
