title: projr compatibility and change log
text:
Relationship: unverified runtime parity; same documented intent. The R README and thesis design describe development previews separately from publication. This is evidence of intent, not proof that every R development path is inert.
Decision/rationale: keep CLI-managed release/version/archive changes out of previews so researchers can inspect development results without publishing.
Implemented: PR123, merged 5d145293e596c5797e9620bd3f00978fa6f99411; Dev-gated VERSION writes, cleanup, document promotion, local export and ignore updates in build.rs, env.rs and yml.rs.
Executed evidence: three-platform Rust tests, including test_preview_safety.rs, and installer checks passed on reviewed head 5d3ac227f52b33fd0c32fddd479cb7296c4072a5. A disposable installed-CLI Python fixture reproduced the previous version/output/ignore mutations.
Gaps: cooperating Python scripts only; renderer YAML rewriting, automatic output isolation, repeated runs, same-project concurrency and full production lifecycle behavior were not established. Subprocesses are not a sandbox.

title: projr compatibility and change log
text:
Relationship: new explicit contract; renderer parity unverified. R path.R dynamically discovers a root, while the thesis defines the project workflow.
Decision/rationale: current approved behavior supersedes defects and stale architecture claims. Root/path defaults must agree across projr, quarto::quarto_render() and RStudio QMD Render. Quarto root equals proj root; nested Quarto projects are unsupported. Direct rendering does not imply release lifecycle parity; R Markdown Knit is a separate entrypoint.
Implemented: PR124, merged 635aa9efac0d7a28971236ab78c879b21be5ec31, corrected AGENTS/README/flow guidance and added the behavior contract. This was documentation, not renderer code.
Executed evidence: independent document review and remote Rust CI passed at dbf8d5fd94a87bba32ffc95cd2ee3b47f1e04277.
Gaps: no direct R frontend, Quarto/RStudio GUI or fresh-render-session parity test was performed. No projr production code or thesis text was changed.

title: projr compatibility and change log
text:
Relationship: different root-resolution mechanism; new CLI selection. R path.R calls root discovery from current context. The CLI now captures one absolute root and passes it to each managed child as PROJ_PROJECT_ROOT.
Decision/rationale: explicit selection wins, and path queries must not change projects after cwd changes. This deliberately improves unstable root behavior rather than copying it.
Implemented: PR125, merged f265eb46c91a300fe0aafad3119d998038946a0b; project.rs, ignore.rs, main.rs and build.rs. Direct library builds configure each child command instead of mutating the caller’s process-global root.
Executed evidence: three-platform tests at 779b3010040eeb23f08434478e0812173eb2a723 cover explicit precedence, spaces, invalid roots, changed cwd and overlapping builds in two distinct roots.
Gaps: marker discovery was not changed; R path helpers and direct render entrypoints do not yet consume this captured context. The tests do not promise general environment isolation or same-project concurrent builds.

title: projr compatibility and change log
text:
Relationship: same static read-only configuration intent; runtime R parity unverified. R yml.R reads/merges configuration; this does not establish equivalence of every R public path helper or its cache routing.
Decision/rationale: reading configuration or paths must not update ignore files. Mutating build/init operations request synchronization explicitly, and bad configuration must not replace custom ignores with default rules.
Implemented: PR126, merged cd34c3208f1ed1c3c27571e7ce2828498a4aecdb; yml.rs, build.rs, init.rs/main.rs.
Executed evidence: three-platform tests at cc132f1e1b288c7560ff6b6b06fcac369a475355 snapshot files/directories for CLI queries, exercise direct API reads and production ignore synchronization, and preserve custom ignores on malformed/read-failing config. Permission-denied coverage ran on Linux/macOS.
Gaps: supported aliases, unknown-option handling and effective merged script/hook configuration remained unchanged and incomplete.

title: projr compatibility and change log
text:
Relationship: new CLI transport contract; same failure-reporting intent. R build-engine.R uses R errors; that is not a process exit-code protocol for language wrappers.
Decision/rationale: a printed error must not be returned as successful execution. Failed Git remote inspection must not proceed to GitHub creation.
Implemented: PR127, merged 8e955b32bc1f611d38a8931d489de2bdfc50d5c7; main.rs routes operation failures to nonzero status and init.rs propagates previously swallowed external failures.
Executed evidence: three-platform tests at a741b5f9de63dcb96ca527607105e5547be1da7c cover failing queries/version/init/ ignores, missing executables, child failure and successful queries. Local fake Git/GitHub commands on Linux/macOS made no network requests.
Gaps: structured error/capability protocols and clean/idempotent Git-init coverage remained open; failure status is not rollback or R-runtime parity.

title: projr compatibility and change log
text:
Relationship: new CLI mode. The R baseline’s build-engine.R calls dependency helpers; no equivalent explicit CLI flag/parity is claimed.
Decision/rationale: machine invocations must not need the CLI’s prompts or automatic package installation. Controlled child stdin must actually be closed.
Implemented: PR128, merged f7ff7e92451a3174d6cb9c5fd60151621e66bd04 after independent review at 5dedee7da69cbe52837993e86bc4837c4c3342a1; adds the flag, inherited mode, runner stdin closure and controlled R-probe stdin closure.
Executed evidence: three-platform tests and installer checks passed at that head; fake-R EOF/no-install tests ran on Linux/macOS and Python runner-stdin coverage ran on all three platforms.
Gaps: no actual R startup/renderer execution comparison; initialization retains existing requested-operation defaults and third-party code can ignore EOF. This does not establish general subprocess isolation.

title: projr compatibility and change log
text:
Relationship: same absent-dev fallback; different explicit-empty guarantee. R yml-scripts.R falls back when dev scripts are absent. Empty-list behavior also passes through validation and renderer selection, so a reliable R upload-only no-analysis contract has not been demonstrated.
Decision/rationale: explicit [] selects no analysis, preserving hooks and production upload/export; absence still falls back. It must not discover or render unrequested files. Cleanup/promotion must preserve upload inputs.
Implementation status: PR129 removes the Dev-empty error and derives one analysis-selection guard for renderer setup/cleanup/promotion. tests/test_empty_scripts.rs checks hooks, existing output/docs bytes, actual production archive bytes and preview nonpublication.
Executed evidence: three-platform Rust tests and installer checks passed at f4b3739554dc548911019c450ca1e90a196d33d2; independent review inspected those logs and cleared that code head. The documentation-only final head 999b730fd2cc23215e4a07a1231d7d6fa3543966 passed all nine checks in runs 39486028024/39486028097 and independent review. Merged as 5617a6daed1f4743a9b2609694a2f84ad4c902eb; post-merge test, installer and site runs 39486858711/39486858532/39486858701 passed.
Gaps: YAML null-as-absence and malformed-list validation were inspected in source, not newly exercised by this policy slice. No R runtime empty-list parity test or real renderer execution is claimed.
Confirmed but separate runtime gaps: retain projr markers (including README/ VERSION), accept legacy _projr.yml with a both-base-files error, and use local > profiles > base with earlier profiles first. The R precedence evidence is yml.R. These approvals are recorded in the behavior contract; this change does not implement aliases, marker expansion or merged script/hook context.

title: projr compatibility and change log
text:
The actual .agents/skills/ponytail/SKILL.md is vendored unchanged from DietrichGebert/ponytail v4.10.0, upstream commit e3ba2aa6f1e6f0bc4d69eb09c9f0d0a93af56156, as installed by PR121. Its pinned upstream bytes and the existing projcli, projr, setupmjr and projects copies all have SHA-256 1316a2f3f95741d2300b116fe0c2d81ce4a9568656ed0a62643f54aaf09957f2. The established setupmjr vendoring contract matches; no duplicate or replacement skill was installed.
The skill prescribes the full-mode simplicity ladder, tracing callers before changing shared behavior, reusing existing code/stdlib/dependencies, and leaving an appropriate runnable check. It supplies no separate executable review script. Applying that guidance is a self-review, separate from independent review and CI.
Completed-chunk review of PR128 at 5dedee7da69cbe52837993e86bc4837c4c3342a1:

Traced the prompt helpers, main description prompt, dependency probes, install branch, script/hooks and project-render runners. Reused the existing EnvGuard, one shared mode predicate and standard-library null stdin; no dependency or custom execution framework was introduced.

All three remote Rust suites and installers passed; this self-review remained separate from the independent exact-head review.

Completed-chunk review of PR129’s empty-selection change:

Reused the existing explicit-list resolver and pipeline; no new execution framework, configuration key or dependency was added.
Traced preflight, version, cleanup, hooks, document promotion and publication. Finding: skipping script execution alone could still erase upload-only inputs or require unused renderers. Action: derive one shared analysis-selection guard and apply it before those stages; keep hooks/publication outside that guard.
Retained data-preservation and failure handling. Added runnable integration checks for real archive bytes and absence-versus-empty semantics; those checks passed on all three remote platforms at the code head recorded above. No R runtime parity was inferred.

title: projr compatibility and change log
text:
Relationship: same static projr marker intent; deliberate extensions. projr path.R at 3ac2959 combines VCS, VERSION, README, R-package, RStudio, renv and Quarto criteria. Exact structured-marker patterns were checked in rprojroot root.R at 4d2f450.
Decision/rationale: retain those markers with nearest-wins; remove Rust’s VERSION-first/five-extra-ancestors heuristic. Add pyproject.toml and Julia Project.toml/JuliaProject.toml as requested language extensions. Proj config files also anchor a configured project without VERSION. Requirements/orphan manifests do not create roots. Explicit selection still wins.
Implementation/evidence status: root_from now tests each ancestor once, never child projects. tests/test_root_markers.rs covers retained marker patterns, invalid structured markers, weak/nested markers, deep invocation, explicit override and a configured Python preview with shallow enumeration. At code head a0d459c5b3a31437443832436535b70d34838553, all nine checks passed in runs 39487247962/39487247928. No R-runtime parity is claimed.
Gaps: required active config, explicit used-directory mappings, early unsupported-setting validation, legacy config-content aliases and full frontend/renderer parity are separate changes. A marker does not claim a Julia runner exists.
Ponytail full-mode review: reused the public root_from entrypoint, existing regex dependency and standard filesystem APIs, replacing the old special-case traversal instead of adding a discovery framework. Traced explicit/inherited precedence and all root callers. Kept discovery read-only and shallow, with runnable positive/negative predicates and workflow coverage; no new dependency.

title: projr compatibility and change log
text:
Relationship: different from prior convenience-default assumptions. The initial Rust/projr-style defaults and historical no-config fixtures are no longer the target behavior. Builds require active root-level configuration and explicit used-directory mappings; init may write familiar defaults into that file, but runtime must not invent missing directories or unknown subpaths.
Decision status: approved. The agreed _proj.yml / legacy _projr.yml names apply; explicitly activated profile files may provide configuration, while inactive profiles alone do not satisfy the requirement. Cwd discovery fallback does not waive build validation. Unknown behavior-affecting settings must fail before mutation.
Failure/publication target: restore pre-build state except permitted cache residue; storage/publication retry must not rerun or mislabel analysis. Existing staging/version/publication behavior does not yet prove that transaction.
Evidence/gaps: earlier CI entries remain accurate historical evidence for their source commits, not acceptance of the superseded no-config/default-path policy. Future fixtures must declare used paths and active configuration. The current core still needs enforcement and failure tests for the new rules.
Authorship boundary: the existing R package is entirely off limits, including root-helper fixes. A later backend port/integration must establish R parity; no such work or runtime comparison is claimed here. Thesis text remains untouched.

title: projr compatibility and change log
text:
Relationship: same projr local > profiles > base precedence, with earlier-listed profiles winning; legacy _projr.yml is accepted alongside canonical _proj.yml as an explicit compatibility decision. Both base files together fail instead of silently merging. Source comparison remains projr yml.R at 3ac2959.
Implemented: shared base selection for merged reads, existing build base inspection, parameters insertion and local-profile cloning. Explicit profile lists replace ambient lists; traversal-like explicit names fail validation. Profile/local files retain their existing _projr- names in this bounded slice.
Evidence: new runnable query/alias/ambiguity/preservation/precedence tests passed on all three platforms at 53463d325c85c538ae0b8a5e792caa6bc997e452. All nine checks in runs 39488461110/39488461213 passed; independent review inspected alias, precedence and duplicate-key logs and cleared that head. Final documentation/instruction head c8b208f9243f828de05977f8e76d6f2074535a9b passed all nine checks in runs 39489639669/39489639654 and independent review; merged as 0fec2735355ee5e9b9ba64d33ecd4796bf396301. Post-merge checks passed. No R runtime tests.
Gaps: one merged build script/hook context, active-configuration requirement, explicit directory mappings and early unsupported-setting validation remain separate work. This does not claim builds yet satisfy those approved rules.
Ponytail full-mode review: traced base filename readers and reused one stdlib path selector; reversed existing deep-merge traversal rather than adding a merger or dependency. Preserved null-as-absence and explicit-empty-list behavior. Checks exercise real query results and preservation on ambiguity.

PR131 failure-path review found that direct YAML-to-JSON deserialization allowed duplicate keys to overwrite earlier values. Restored YAML Value parsing before JSON conversion, preserving duplicate-key rejection at every active layer. Added top-level and nested duplicate-key regressions for both base filenames, profile and local files, including CLI failure before preview state writes. The prior green CI did not cover this malformed-input case; the corrected head above passed the new checks and independent re-review. Ponytail review kept this at the shared file parser rather than guarding individual callers.

title: projr compatibility and change log
text:
Relationship: new/unverified design. The durable CRAN note records the discussed future R-code wrapper around a separately installed CLI, meaningful unconditional R-only/mocked tests, conditional executable integration on CRAN, and mandatory pinned/checksummed CLI integration in our own CI. It cites current policy and pinned Quarto precedent.
No existing R code or tests were changed; no CRAN submission, agreement, preinstalled executable, automatic-download exemption or renderer parity is claimed. Implementation and runtime validation remain future work.
Ponytail full-mode design review: kept one linked design note; reused the repository’s behavior/compatibility/AGENTS pointers. No installer, wrapper, binding, mock framework or external contact was added speculatively.

title: projr compatibility and change log
text:
Relationship: follows projr’s merged-configuration intent and the approved local > earlier profiles > later profiles > base precedence. The prior Rust pipeline validated merged settings but separately reread the base for execution.
Implemented: deserialize and validate one merged value, then select scripts and hooks from it. Explicit empty dev selection remains empty; absence falls back to build settings. Both base filenames use this same execution path. Configuration parsing/validation, target resolution and preflight now precede production environment-ignore writes.
Evidence: runnable Python fixtures check conflicting profiles, legacy base, local dev overrides and hook results, plus invalid merged configuration with a local environment file and missing-target failures leaving ignores/version/cache untouched. Remote CI and independent review pending; no real R/renderer execution is claimed.
Gaps: required active config, explicit mappings, all unsupported-field rejection and transactional rollback remain separate approved work. Environment loading still uses the existing process-global guard; this change makes no new same-process concurrent environment guarantee.
Ponytail full-mode review: removed the second base-only YAML parser and its ignored parse failure instead of adding a second configuration model. Reused existing typed validation and dev fallback rules. Traced validation, selection, hooks and environment-ignore writes; retained explicit error propagation.

title: projr compatibility and change log
text: The 2026-10-20 static audit records the pinned baseline, reported failure paths, required regressions and correction order. Its findings are not runtime reproductions or completed fixes. Highest managed-state risks remain blockers to production-safety claims; arbitrary external script effects are outside managed rollback. No mechanical edition upgrade or CAS redesign is claimed. This review uses the actual Ponytail full-mode skill to prioritize root causes and data-preservation checks over cosmetic rewriting.

title: projr compatibility and change log
text:
Relationship: deliberate difference from projr convenience defaults, as explicitly approved. Every build requires a base file or activated profile; inactive profile/local files alone do not qualify. Discovery still falls back to cwd independently. Empty analysis is valid with active configuration.
Implemented: build gate before writes; unsupported typed configuration fields fail instead of disappearing in a top-level filter. Build failures include their error causes so unsupported-field diagnostics name the field. Arbitrary parameter and metadata maps remain supported and parameter aliases reach validation.
Evidence: runnable tests cover active/base/legacy/inactive/local/no-config cases, unsupported nested keys, dynamic maps and no pre-build state writes. Remote CI/independent review pending. Explicit directory enforcement is still a separate gap; this does not yet establish transaction/promotion safety.
Ponytail full-mode review: reused Serde’s unknown-field validation and the existing active profile resolver; removed silent filtering from runtime reads. No new parser/schema/dependency. Kept the old public filter helper only for compatibility; runtime no longer uses it.

PR134 merged-context evidence: exact head 29b2bdfb564f3193a0e93eb43096f89f2691653a passed all nine checks in runs 39490264159/39490264169. Independent review inspected the three new regressions across platforms and cleared the bounded change. Merged as eb1204026e8809780fc783f27b0be7edf9b5033e. Preflight itself is not guaranteed read-only; environment/profile-source unification, per-run environment safety, strict directories and transaction/promotion safety remain open. This evidence is batched with the substantive active-configuration change to avoid an extra matrix.
PR135 review found mixed parameter aliases survived per-file parsing as separate keys and then conflicted at typed deserialization. Canonicalize the one accepted alias to parameters in the shared reader before merging. New fixtures cover all 64 base/profile/local alias combinations, earlier-profile precedence and retained nested values; same-file multiple aliases and YAML duplicate keys remain errors. Ponytail full-mode re-review kept the fix at the shared loader, without caller guards or a second merge model. Exact amended CI/re-review remain required.

title: projr compatibility and change log
text:
Relationship: new safety checks, not a blanket ban on external resources. Before production analysis cleanup, reject root/ancestor destinations, staging and resource overlaps, selected-input containment, VCS metadata, label path separators and symlinked managed-write paths. Directory replacement also requires an existing source and disjoint destination before deleting bytes.
Evidence: runnable preservation fixtures cover root, ancestor, staging, raw/output overlaps, traversal labels, Unix symlink parents and low-level self/ancestor/nested/missing-source moves. Remote CI/review pending.
Limits: does not yet provide atomic promotion or complete rollback, protect against concurrent hostile filesystem replacement, undo user-script external effects or establish full CAS integrity. External disjoint paths remain valid.
Ponytail full-mode review: one stdlib identity resolver shared by build and promotion guards; trace all promotion callers, retain explicit errors instead of silently accepting missing source/read errors. No new dependency.

Path-guard Ponytail re-review traced the public cleanup helpers as well as build: direct clear_pre/clear_post now apply the shared destination checks, clear_old rejects symlinked staging parents, and traversal-bearing version components fail before cache deletion. Label separator validation lives in shared typed validation for all modes. Generic destructive move APIs require resolved parents and reject symlink aliases; positive direct-API fixtures canonicalize their temporary roots so macOS system temp aliases do not violate that explicit safety precondition. Added a direct-cleanup preservation fixture. This is not complete transactional restoration or a guarantee against concurrent filesystem replacement.
PR135 final evidence (batched with path guards): code head 3839173366e55cffa946ea0e2afe4757ae48e77d passed all alias/conflict regressions on three platforms and independent re-review. Base-update head abc62f966766915093351c00a6a1724a0d1b69da changed no executable/tests/Cargo code, preserved the published site, passed all ten checks in runs 39492001512/39492001479/39492001493 and focused independent review. Merged as a0909e413915847498e77669a3b669941dbfe3fe. Required active config and unsupported field rejection are implemented; explicit used-directory enforcement and finite control-value validation remain separate gaps.
PR137 independent review found that configured-root checks alone missed derived version/output cache leaves. Validate all actual cleanup bases before the first deletion, including configured-cache and legacy staging paths. Direct dev cleanup is now a true no-op. The same review traced individual document promotion and recursive copying: validate paths before creating directories or renaming files, require actual outputs, reject traversal/aliasing and prevalidate asset moves. The two duplicate individual-renderer helpers now reuse one guarded implementation. Added targeted direct-API regressions; amended remote CI/re-review are required. This does not yet fix build callers discarding promotion errors or provide full restoration/atomicity; those remain the following focused work.
The repaired PR137 guard prevalidates concrete generated-file/asset paths and both legacy/configured cache-derived leaves before VERSION/ignore writes, including dangling links. Individual and project promotion now resolve the configured docs destination rather than a root/docs fallback; Python-only builds do not clear unrelated docs. Unix fake-Quarto/fake-R CLI fixtures exercise the reported linked root/docs sentinel bypass and actual successful external promotion, without a real renderer installation. Direct helper tests remain cross-platform.
Project-render source safety is explicitly conservative: recognized source-like .qmd, .Rmd, .md and .ipynb files or links in managed cleanup trees cause an early error. This can reject generated Markdown there; it is not exact Quarto or Bookdown input discovery. Keep sources and managed destinations separate until a renderer-provided input plan is supported. Quarto’s documented project input types are described in Project Basics.
The prepared literal-root glob fix is included in PR137 because a metacharacter root otherwise hides explicit inputs from the cleanup containment guard. Reuse glob::Pattern::escape for the root prefix only, retaining user include/exclude syntax. Runnable tests verify actual analysis bytes and selected-input preservation under a bracket-containing root. This is the same audited root-cause fix, not an additional discovery policy or dependency. Existing standalone preparation remains preserved and must not later be merged as duplicate work.
Windows CI at 9938173 exposed a skipped explicit failing script. Source review of glob 0.3.3 confirmed that escaping the canonical Windows namespace changes its filesystem prefix. Normalize Disk/UNC namespaces for glob transport only, keep filesystem prefixes literal, escape only directory components and join patterns using native path operations. The captured root is unchanged. Explicit include patterns with no files now fail instead of reporting successful no-op execution. New native/canonical-root execution markers run on every platform; network UNC execution remains unverified.
The same review found generated filenames could overwrite another selected script or hook, DESCRIPTION or environment configuration. Before renderer invocation, compare all concrete output/asset paths against the complete selected-input set and reject authoritative project/environment metadata filenames. Fake-renderer fixtures prove those failures happen before scripts, VERSION or ignore writes. Amended exact-head CI and independent re-review remain required.

title: projr compatibility and change log
text:
Different (approved): runtime directory resolution requires declared nonempty paths and never invents missing labels or suffix subpaths. This supersedes earlier in-memory directory-default behavior, including read-only path queries. Missing configuration can still be queried as an empty inventory; builds require active configuration. Storage content labels must exist, and relative storage locations resolve against the captured root. Selected cleanup and project-render staging require cache; upload-only empty analysis does not require an unused cache mapping. Rendered documentation requires docs. Cache cleanup uses the declared mapping, not a parallel hard-coded _tmp tree.
Same preset / different timing: pinned projr 3ac29595d0e39552495d863661b99ea015d59d3d, R/yml-dir.R:334–345, supplies raw-data: _raw_data, cache: _tmp, output: _output. Rust local-only proj --project . --non-interactive init directories writes those explicit paths once when no base/active profile exists. Existing configuration stays byte-for-byte intact. No scripts field is generated: absence preserves discovery, while an existing explicit empty list stays empty. No Git/GitHub/R setup is invoked. The Rust accepted label-prefix subset still differs from projr’s broader labels; this slice does not claim full schema parity or R frontend changes.
Ponytail full-mode review reused the shared resolver and existing tempfile dependency rather than adding a directory framework. Existing malformed/unreadable config preservation tests remain; new tests cover missing paths, undeclared labels, case collisions, explicit storage references, cache ownership, no-executable local init, preserved base/legacy/profile bytes and actual default-discovered Python output. Remote CI and independent review are pending. Init is not an atomic transaction against filesystem failures or concurrent replacement.
PR137 final eb727912f2f0302d01611cca7b84188d34c34e82 independently cleared; all ten checks passed (runs 39496127892/39496127915/39496127894). Merge 56564b9a4aeeef03ae199b04140b5f3d325b3505 passed post-merge test and installation runs 39496869636/39496869586 and published the site in 39496869590.
Independent PR139 review removed an over-broad production cache prerequisite. Only selected operations that consume cache require its mapping. Explicit empty analysis can export declared existing results without cache/docs mappings. An explicit Python-only selection does not activate a renderer merely because its project marker exists. The custom-cache fixture now executes Python and checks actual custom staging cleanup plus preserved legacy _tmp bytes. Fake-R fixtures declare docs while retaining EOF/no-install assertions. These amendments require fresh remote checks and exact-head re-review.

title: projr compatibility and change log
text:
Same precedence / deliberate error handling difference: inherited OS values win over local, earlier environment profiles, then base assignments. Preserve non-Unicode inherited values rather than treating them as absent. Reject empty, equals-containing or NUL keys and NUL values before calling OS mutation APIs. Read whole files with propagated errors rather than lines().flatten(); required file errors and directory inputs cannot silently bypass validation or loop. Diagnostics include paths/line numbers, never assignment values. Same-file validation finishes before assignments from that file are applied. Ignore writes in explicit activation occur only after validation succeeds.
Ponytail full-mode review traced all load/assignment callers and reused existing configuration-entry presence checks. No parser dependency was added. Prepared CLI checks cover invalid/NUL entries, directory and permission-denied required files, secret-free diagnostics, actual inherited/local/profile/base child values and no analysis invocation on errors. Remote checks/review are pending.
This bounded fix does not make EnvGuard thread-safe: process-global environment mutation remains a known risk until per-run values and profiles reach all child commands and Git/preflight consumers. No credential handling or CAS code changes. ## Prepared managed-state restoration invariant (not yet verified)
The restoration implementation under preparation replaces the legacy middle-only catch and synthesized development-version rollback. Before controlled production mutations, capture exact bytes, permissions and absence for VERSION, ignore files, root configuration/state and existing root regular files; selected in-project inputs; declared output/docs directory trees; and concrete individual renderer output/asset paths. Capture initially absent parent directories too. Declared external output/docs paths are supported. Raw data, Git internals, arbitrary external user-script effects and cache contents are not backed up. Managed trees containing symlinks or unsupported entries are rejected rather than followed.
Backups use existing tempfile and streaming std::fs copies in private OS temporary recovery storage outside disposable project cache. No project mapping is invented, and cache-free upload-only operations remain supported. Recovery sources are copied to temporary restore staging before any current target is removed. Missing recovery bytes leave intact current state alone and are reported as unavailable.
One local failure boundary covers ignore synchronization, cleanup, all pre/both/ post hooks, engine configuration, execution, output promotion and VERSION writing. Promotion errors propagate; renderer configuration is restored byte-for-byte on success and failure. VERSION changes only after hooks/render/promotion succeed. Failures and caught panics restore captured state. All restore entries are attempted; if restoration fails, retain recovery bytes and report both the original failure and restoration failures with the backup path. Substituted links are rejected.
After local success, storage export/Git publication form a separate failure phase: publication failure reports successful local analysis and retains the new local release. Export precedes requested post-output cleanup so archives contain actual build bytes. A failure during this later cleanup is explicitly reported as such; there is no external publication rollback. No pre-build Git snapshot or second post-build commit is needed. Upstream selection/native credentials and publication retry identity remain separate unfinished work.
Prepared checks cover each hook/analysis failure, initially absent VERSION, exact old output/docs bytes and empty directories, renderer execution/missing promotion, exact YAML comments/render lists, restore-failure backup retention with external sentinels, and successful local analysis followed by failed storage publication. These are unrun: no local compilation under memory pressure; remote CI and independent review are still required. No power-loss atomicity, concurrent-writer or global script-side-effect guarantee is claimed. M2 attempt/release records and analysis-free retry commands remain open.
PR141 review corrections: normalize selected-input identities before comparing root containment (including Windows namespace forms); require nonempty supported document artifacts before project promotion; remove prior expected individual artifacts and project staging immediately before rendering. New regressions cover nested scripts/hooks modifying or deleting themselves, empty renderer staging, stale individual artifacts, cache purge during failed analysis, and unavailable recovery bytes without further deletion. These amendments require fresh remote CI and independent review. Project artifact scanning remains a conservative supported-document check, not a complete renderer manifest guarantee.
Further review keeps project promotion conservative: require a freshly created tree containing a nonempty supported document, rather than guessing per-input filenames from incomplete document-only format metadata. Fake PDF rendering tests cover explicit and inherited project formats. Complete expected-output manifests remain unimplemented; individual document format inference is still a separate known limitation. Selected managed script/hook paths reject symlinks along the original path before canonical identity comparison. System recovery temp anchors are canonicalized, including cache-free operations, without weakening user-path symlink rejection.
Bookdown’s framework-controlled <book_filename>_files source/destination are resolved and guarded before writes, with default _main and portable custom stems. Their exact prior bytes/presence join the recovery set. A fake successful render followed by a failing post-hook checks both default/custom native asset trees and released docs are restored. Unsupported path-like stems fail instead of traversing outside the project. Remote verification and independent review remain required.

title: projr compatibility and change log
text:
Deliberate implementation change: build_project resolves inherited OS values, explicit profiles, local/earlier-profile/base environment files and required keys without modifying std::env. The same immutable context drives YAML profile selection, clear-output/installation/interaction controls, interpreter dependency probes, scripts/hooks/renderers and existing Git capability/preflight/publication commands. Child commands receive a captured environment, with the resolved project root and intentional script profile values applied per command. Inherited non-Unicode values remain intact. Existing Git credential selection/policy is forwarded, not redesigned.
Prepared remote checks force two library builds with different roots, profiles and fixture values to overlap while an unrelated child observes the unchanged parent. Mock R and Git commands verify probes and execution receive file-supplied values. Existing input/preflight/preview/root-context tests remain. Ponytail full-mode review reuses shared parsers and the standard Command.env_clear/envs API, with no global mutex or new dependency. No credentials are formatted through Debug or diagnostics. Remote CI and independent review are pending.
Legacy public EnvGuard activation/assignment APIs and CLI startup guards still mutate process state and are explicitly not safe concurrent environment APIs. The guarantee is bounded to the build path and commands receiving this context; unrelated external code that concurrently mutates std::env remains outside it. Native Git authentication/upstream policy and broader environment sanitization are separate unfinished work. R package and CAS code are unchanged.
PR143 Windows review correction: inherited native keys/values are passed through, but non-ASCII assignment/required keys in environment files are rejected early with a precise diagnostic. This deliberately bounded support avoids approximating Windows Unicode case identity and allowing a file alias to override an inherited key. ASCII case precedence and native non-Unicode values retain their dedicated platform tests. Unicode alias rejection is tested on Windows before analysis or authoritative writes; complete Unicode assignment-key support is not claimed.

title: projr compatibility and change log
text:
Different/new, approved root policy: relative to pinned projr 3ac29595d0e39552495d863661b99ea015d59d3d (R/engine.R, R/path.R) and the audited Rust script-parent cwd, scripts/hooks now start in the captured root. Shallow default enumeration and explicitly selected nested paths are preserved. Quarto uses its supported --execute-dir; individual R Markdown supplies knit_root_dir. R Markdown filenames are trailing data arguments to fixed R code, avoiding apostrophe/source interpolation. See Rscript arguments, rmarkdown render, and Quarto render controls.
Different/new, conservative supported subset: native R Markdown output and Quarto format select one known format; PDF/Word no longer guess HTML. Unknown or multiple formats, individual inherited metadata/unsupported output layouts, document-rendering hooks and nested Quarto roots fail early. This deliberately rejects previously guessed/unsafe layouts rather than claiming full renderer support. clear_output and ignore choices are finite early-validated values. No R production code changes, direct IDE verification or automatic preview isolation are included.
Ponytail full-mode review traced execution/preflight/promotion callers and reused existing YAML, command/environment and path safety facilities without new dependencies. Remote regressions are prepared for real nested Python hook/script ordering and cwd, safe R argument transport, HTML/PDF/Word promotion, nested roots, invalid controls and unsupported layouts preserving config/VERSION. CI and independent review are pending. PR144 exact head 344bddc4b82eb810b339e475eeb6824b1ef56bac passed independent review and all ten checks; merged 6c0079fb78b4f3f84df50423dae81c4b4a0e0f16 and post-merge workflows 39508879381/39508879332/39508879482 passed. Git clearance is bounded optional publication, not a complete release-readiness guarantee.

title: projr compatibility and change log
text:
Different/new: the audited Rust baseline scanned/hash-named files, reopened them for copy, trusted existing objects, normalized Unix literal backslashes into slashes, accepted missing/file sources as empty snapshots and treated manifest existence as verification. This slice rejects missing/non-directory sources and unsafe overlap, linked/unsupported entries, ambiguous logical paths and malformed/non-ASCII digests before unsafe lookup. Literal backslash names are rejected rather than conflated with nested paths. Original source bytes are read only.
Hash the exact stream copied into temporary storage; validate existing object bytes before trusting the digest key. Immutable objects/manifests publish without clobber; manifest conflicts fail instead of truncating existing bytes. Manifest inspection parses/validates JSON and filename hash; file inspection hashes referenced objects. Index replacement uses complete staged bytes with CSV escaping for label/version. Temp fixtures use canonical physical paths so macOS system temp aliases do not silently weaken user-controlled symlink checks.
Ponytail full-mode review reuses BLAKE3, tempfile, shared path guards and standard streaming I/O. No new dependency or CAS schema/version-identity redesign. Prepared remote checks cover malformed paths/digests, Unix backslash collisions, missing/file sources, corrupt existing objects, changed source paths during stream copy, injected read errors, immutable manifest conflict and index failure with old state preserved, CSV metadata escaping and actual referenced-object hashes. Existing empty-directory and dedup/version-sensitive manifest tests remain. Remote CI/review are pending.
This advances existing MiguelRodo/issues#688–690 rather than creating duplicate roadmap issues. Broader CAS lifecycle/GC, a consistent concurrent-source snapshot, multi-writer index updates and crash durability remain open. Failed index publication may leave a complete unindexed manifest; object residue is valid but not a successful indexed export. There is no full cross-filesystem metadata transaction or global scientific reproducibility guarantee. Existing R package remains untouched.
PR145 review adds shared manifest file/directory prefix-collision validation. Logical files a and a/b cannot coexist, independent of input order or intervening names. Both inspection strategies are tested with real digest-matching objects so the rejection proves layout validation, not an unrelated missing-object failure.
CAS metadata readers/writers require regular files before reading existing manifest or index bytes; Unix named-pipe regressions use a bounded completion check so hostile special metadata cannot block verification or ingestion indefinitely.

title: projr compatibility and change log
text:
Different/new (approved explicit-action policy): no commit/fetch/push/token requirement is inferred from Git metadata. Omitted commits and not_behind checks are off; explicit actions use the per-run environment. Commit builds fail before writes when Git already contains changes, preserving unrelated work; staged-index no-op is success. Publish one HEAD refspec to the configured current upstream, never origin/main. Custom pushRemote/pushDefault/remote.push routing is conservatively rejected early rather than silently choosing the wrong destination. Local release success remains distinct from publication failure. The retained reference projr and legacy Rust are evidence, not authority for these newer confirmed decisions.
Native Git authentication is default. Explicit use_proj_cred_helper enables only existing single-line environment tokens on standard HTTPS github.com remotes; no build calls GitHub CLI token discovery. Fixed helper code accepts only HTTPS github.com credential requests; the token is quoted environment data, not argv or shell source. The helper list resets for that one command; no persistent config or credentials are created. Captured network failures report status without reflecting potential secret stderr. Other hosts use native configured authentication. See Git’s credential helper protocol and upstream/refspec documentation.
Ponytail full-mode review reuses native Git, existing providers and shared environment context. No new dependency or credential store. Prepared remote checks use fake Git/GH to cover zero implicit calls, configured fetch only, real upstream/refspec, no-op/single commit, dirty-input preservation, native versus opt-in helper behavior, host/protocol denial, punctuation as literal token data, helper reset and secret-free argv/diagnostics. No real network/auth action is tested. Remote CI and independent review are pending; CAS integrity and analysis-free publication retries remain open.
PR143 reviewer note: the shared Windows ASCII assignment restriction also applies to public legacy EnvGuard::track_and_set, not just file-based keys. Inherited native environment values remain preserved; the legacy mutation APIs remain outside the build-path concurrency guarantee.
PR144 review guards force untracked-file and submodule visibility during the clean check, reject pushurl and multiple effective push URLs before writes, and disable follow-tags/submodule recursion for the single explicit push. Extra destinations are also checked at dispatch. Git’s executable is resolved explicitly from the per-run PATH (git.exe on Windows), avoiding native parent-PATH fallback in both availability checks and execution. Remote fixtures cover hidden untracked content, fan-out/redirection rejection and explicit suppression flags. Fresh exact-head checks and independent re-review are required.
The same preflight also rejects mirror pushes, absent remotes, multiple tracking merge entries and effective push/fetch endpoint differences (including expanded pushInsteadOf). Destination inspection uses get-url –push –all before controlled build writes. Native Git configuration is read only; no remote/auth settings are rewritten. Fake regressions assert each unsupported case preserves VERSION and unrelated private bytes and never reaches add/commit/fetch/push.
Captured push identity includes checked-out branch, upstream remote/ref and expanded effective endpoint, without Debug exposure. Revalidate the complete supported identity immediately before commit and again before push. Hook/script changes to URL, pushurl, mirror, branch, ref or remote fail publication without redirecting the push; successful local VERSION/output are retained. Fake regressions switch those values after an analysis marker and assert no add/commit/push occurs. This guards within-run mutation, not an atomic lock against concurrent external Git changes.
The sibling public post_build_sync API now uses the same captured-context checked publication helper as build_project. A fake commit hook changing the endpoint is rejected before push. Explicit Git lookup anchors directories absolutely but preserves the candidate leaf spelling, supporting symlink-based name dispatchers; a fake git-to-dispatcher symlink regression prevents argv[0] canonicalization regressions.

title: projr compatibility and change log
text:
Different/new: the cooperating-script-only PR123 preview guarantee is extended using reviewed exact-byte recovery from PR141. Captured release output/docs, VERSION/config/root files, selected scripts/hooks, local publication stores and ordinary VCS metadata restore after successful and failing previews. The pinned projr 3ac29595d0e39552495d863661b99ea015d59d3d remains workflow evidence, not a tested runtime parity claim. No R changes or publication calls are introduced.
Bounded: cache artifacts remain; arbitrary undeclared/external script effects, worktree VCS pointer targets, concurrent writes/power loss and automatic redirection of every script output are not covered. Recovery rejects unsafe overlaps/links, preserves original missing/present state and never deletes a current target before its existing recovery bytes are prepared. Restore failure is a failed preview, even when analysis returned zero, and retains available private recovery bytes.
Ponytail full-mode review reused BuildState, filesystem identity/overlap guards and existing command environments without a new transaction framework/dependency. Prepared remote regressions deliberately delete/alter captured outputs, archive, config, selected nested source and VCS state on success/failure, including pre/post hooks with explicit empty analysis. Cache result bytes survive; no framework Git or export calls occur. A missing-backup success path verifies honest failure and safe current-state preservation. CI/independent review pending.
PR148 review uses one resolved cache identity for both private-storage and managed target overlap checks. Dot-dot cache spellings with ancestor/descendant or shared absent-parent publication paths reject before analysis; a disjoint existing-parent case preserves actual cache artifact bytes. Recovery must not remove allowed cache.
Recovery overlap comparisons conservatively fold ASCII names on all platforms, including absent suffixes (Windows/default macOS can alias them). Missing Unicode components reject only when overlap comparison reaches an ambiguous alias; disjoint existing/ASCII directory prefixes rule out overlap before a Unicode output leaf. Actual filesystem paths retain original spelling; these identities only bound overlap and deduplication. Cross-platform absent-case-alias fixtures fail before cache writes.

title: projr compatibility and change log
text:
Different/new: replace stale SATVILab/proj-core download defaults with canonical MiguelRodo/projcli. Require version-bound asset names and exact mandatory SHA256 matches before replacing installed bytes, rather than generic binary fallbacks or optional checksums. User-local destination staging preserves prior bytes on failed download/verification. No system/PATH/auth settings are changed by installation.
Remote builds/tests use Cargo.lock. The existing release workflow becomes a draft-only explicitly labeled preview pipeline for matching reviewed preview tags; it does not mutate version/main, configure APT or publish releases automatically. Linux/Windows x86-64 artifacts are the initial supported delivery scope, not a claim that every platform works. Existing R package remains untouched.
Ponytail full-mode review reuses curl/native PowerShell SHA256 and Python stdlib staging/manifest checks without dependencies or a hosting/packaging framework. Prepared remote checks install the actual CI binaries and reject absent/wrong/ duplicate checksums, corrupted bytes and version mismatches while retaining an existing target. Artifact collection rejects corrupt/missing/duplicate/version- mismatched inputs; help smoke failures are no longer swallowed. CI/review pending. No tag, publication, WSL install, signature or reproducible-build claim yet.

title: projr compatibility and change log
text:
New: protocol-v1 opt-in JSON envelope and capability version, with static structured failure codes/nonzero exits. Existing human CLI remains default. Queries use explicit-root typed APIs rather than stripping progress prose; config validation returns no raw parameter values. Other command families reuse the existing CLI/domain paths in a noninteractive worker, redirecting child stdout and stderr directly to stderr without log buffering. No credentials/config/argv are copied into protocol errors. User/third-party logs are not auto-redacted.
Pinned projr 3ac29595d0e39552495d863661b99ea015d59d3d is the workflow reference; this machine transport is a new language-neutral boundary, not established R API compatibility. No R code changes, finer domain-error taxonomy, release record or publication-retry semantics. Existing anyhow handling remains the domain layer; issue87 is not duplicated by a cross-module error rewrite.
Ponytail full-mode review uses existing clap/serde/anyhow/query/CLI facilities, standard subprocess stream redirection and no new dependencies. Prepared remote tests cover capability negotiation, typed queries without prose/secrets, malformed config/arguments/root, missing interpreter, child failure/logs, local init and version mutation. CI/independent review pending. Managed preview output isolation remains outstanding and is advertised as false, not described as sandboxing.
PR145 re-cleared CAS head 79050b3a46749a561b5a0cf0cca0451ae5532c6e passed all ten checks and merged 0e10b3e66face673fe966ed61b1be6d2eabf5004; post-merge workflows 39510143656/39510143483/39510143388 passed. CAS multi-writer/crash limits remain as previously recorded.
PR147 reviewer regression preserves the CLI option terminator and literal option-like positional values. Worker controls are inserted before --, and only actual machine flags before that boundary are removed; user paths/option values are retained.
PR146 review additionally rejects document/format-specific output extension and library-directory overrides before writes; these are outside the modeled artifact and recovery layout. Windows execution-root fixtures compare filesystem identity, preserving the cwd requirement across ordinary/verbatim path spellings.
Effective ancestor Quarto projects are rejected when they differ from an explicitly selected inner proj root. Every selected document routed through Quarto, including Rmd, receives nested-root validation. Metadata traversal normalizes root/input filesystem identity before stopping, avoiding Windows namespace spelling differences.
Retained Markdown (keep_md / keep-md, including format options) is rejected in individual layouts before rendering. A nested Rmd sibling sentinel regression with an overwrite-capable fake renderer and failing post-hook prevents this untracked framework artifact from damaging existing Markdown outside the recovery plan.
The reviewed Unicode renderer fixture remains supported: comparison-only cache guards stop at disjoint directory prefixes instead of blanket-rejecting missing Unicode output filenames. Existing actual renderer format/promotion tests retain their apostrophe/Unicode inputs; no fixture reduction hides unsupported output.
PR149 review qualifies checkout as refs/tags/ and verifies HEAD against that exact tag in both jobs. Both platform artifacts record the source commit; collection rejects any mismatch with the draft job’s checked-out tag and publishes the source identity with checksums. Same-named branch regression proves the guard. Windows native Cargo/staging failures are checked before cached bytes can reach artifact upload. The tag-only workflow remains unexercised until an authorized reviewed preview tag is actually created; PR CI is not release evidence.

title: projr compatibility and change log
text:

title: projr compatibility and change log
text:
Relationship: new delivery instructions; comparative R runtime unverified. The guide uses the published 0.4.0-preview.1 Rust assets whose exact source, hashes, native smokes and WSL delivery are recorded above. No existing R package, renderer/IDE parity, broad M1/M2 completion or reproducible-build attestation follows from binary availability.

title: projr compatibility and change log
text:
Same/intended: pinned projr90be501 R/version.R107–207 forces a dev component for preview, and159–264 computes release run versions before execution. Rust now plans active/next versions before hooks: preview retains dev (or uses1), release runs incremented version and leaves dev1 after success. Failure/preview restores authoritative bytes. Cache-key formatting is v..-; existing dotted public/file formatting is retained as a documented representation difference, not a cache escape. Current fixed Rust schema does not port projr’s configurable version-format schema.
Different, deliberate: R root rediscovery and bare VERSION I/O are confirmed defects (diagnostic39554636201). A private per-run snapshot pins root, effective profiles, final mappings and active version. Nested CLI queries no longer reload changed YAML/VERSION. No existing R helper consumes it; R/thesis remain untouched.
New selection rule: CLI > PROJR_PROFILE > QUARTO_PROFILE fallback > base/local build.profile default selects once for proj config/environment. Earlier profiles and local precedence retained. Native renderer QUARTO_PROFILE remains separate.
Tests: new remote regressions cover changed cwd into another project, changed YAML/VERSION, external mappings, human/machine queries, explicit other project, profile priority, success/failure/preview and private snapshot lifetime. PR153 exact head3ccf10e independently cleared; all eleven checks passed in tests39559553707, install39559553890 and docs39559553682. Merged1719694; post-merge checks monitored separately. No local build.
Remaining: configured final paths are still returned; safe routing, fragments, auto/relative presentation, explicit render context, native cwd and embedding fallback follow. Renderer staging still uses the old version in this slice. No complete M1/M2 claim or release/install follows from this PR alone.
Ponytail full review: reused NamedTempFile, per-command RunEnvironment and existing version/config types. One small bounded snapshot, no full config/env/ credential serialization, globals, wrapper, crawler or transaction framework. Parent-process concurrency regression remains required; independent review is separate from self-review. Diagnostic evidence: branch488adaf FINDINGS.md and actual embedded-image runs39554636201/39555352442/39556599001.

title: projr compatibility and change log
text:
Same/intended: projr90be501 R/dir-get.R48–86,229–244,284–301 routes safe output/data/docs into first cache-class/version context. Rust preserves merged declaration order and uses v or v- from captured active version, not mutable VERSION. Exact declared labels select stable role leaves; absolute configured external paths remain available through final lookup.
Different, deliberate: docs uses a consistent cache/docs label leaf rather than the historical physical-docs-path suffix/side-effecting getter. Data labels must be explicitly declared; no implicit root/data fallback. Fragments cannot replace/escape the role root. No YAML rewriting or directory creation on query.
Bounded delivery: –target safe is explicit; final remains the intermediate CLI default until production promotion consumes safe outputs. This avoids changing existing analysis behavior before the consumer is fixed. Auto representation, renderer contexts/staging, default switch and native cwd follow separately.
Tests prepared for remote CI: declaration order opposed to alphabetical order, dev/release cache keys, data/docs/exact labels, absolute external mappings, missing config inputs, fragment escape rejection, changed cwd/YAML/VERSION/profile and actual retained cache bytes with released output preserved. Existing per-directory source.local/source.github title references or named inline definitions precede eligible build.local/build.github destinations. A shared referenced definition may be refined inline through the existing deep merge (null still inherits). Destination source:false excludes it; true or a matching label preference beats the first eligible fallback. content:null/false selects nothing, true selects declared non-cache roles, and lists select declared labels. Source/provider/title declaration order is preserved. No retry switches to another configured source after lookup/download fails.
A valid root manifest.csv is required, matching projr’s prior-build gate. Labels with no recorded files and advertised empty variants skip without clearing. CSV history is not used as an integrity/trust proof. Full sources stage before the existing merge/clear installer; –clear never removes files before a source has been found and copied. Default merge preserves destination-only files. Machine results disclose restored/skipped, selected provider/title/version and destination; failures keep protocol stdout structured with static error text. Stderr carries the operational diagnostic chain, including paths and parser details; it is not a general configuration-redaction boundary. HTTP errors omit credentials and response bodies.
This deliberately fixes R source-selection indexing/inline-definition bugs and clear-before-lookup data loss. It does not add R’s implicit hard-coded archive fallback: undeclared remotes/paths are errors under the agreed explicit mapping contract. Nonempty get policy mappings fail explicitly rather than pretending that R’s ineffective get.strategy/get.conflict controls work. Send policy is not executed by restore. Definitions retain local path versus GitHub title/tag id semantics, including spaces and @version tag normalization.
Boundary: ordinary inline remote/source fields are accepted by this command’s read-only configuration projection only. Normal build validation still rejects unsupported ordinary publication fields, preventing silently ignored uploads. Configured automatic publication, cue/history policy integration, all-label default restore, complete credential-helper fallback and the issue706 registry remain subsequent work. Installed preview remains unchanged.
Pinned comparison: restore gate/selection/download, inline destination defaults, content eligibility. Ponytail full reuses merged YAML, typed core validation, CSV decoding, numeric version comparison and guarded local/ZIP installers. No backend trait, new registry or persistence schema. Filesystem and mocked REST actual CLI fixtures cover source priority, references/inline/profiles, destination preference, numeric archives, VERSION ZIP latest, clear/merge/empty and corrupt failure preservation. No actual GitHub Release mutation or local heavy test is performed. PR183 passed independent review at44478558d0ef41660d513a3f7d74fe399684b245, all12checks and the full pinned gate. It merged ascee85a164fa43cb827c0db69814199994fa4ea66 with an identical tested tree.
Configured restore uses the shared profile selection order: explicit profile, PROJR_PROFILE, QUARTO_PROFILE, then build.profile, with earlier profiles winning and local overrides last. Machine failures preserve installation/recovery details on stderr, including retained backup paths; stdout stays a structured failure. Legacy data CSV rows and remote data namespaces are read without rewriting history; ambiguous canonical/legacy namespaces fail before installation. One optional VERSION trust marker is accepted; it is not a byte-verification claim.
Review precision: VERSION.zip requires exactly the canonical VERSION member spelling, including on case-insensitive filesystems. Metadata transfer staging also closes explicitly and reports cleanup failure paths.

title: projr compatibility and change log
text:
The configured local latest/file matrix now follows each of the8strategy/cue builds with actual machine CLI restore, using configured destination fallback and VERSION discovery. It deliberately damages local bytes/adds a local-only file, then checks explicit clear restores exactly the strategy’s remote bytes while project CSV/VERSION remain unchanged. An advertised empty snapshot preserves local-only bytes. This is a real local-filesystem round trip, not just upload success, mock transport, or an actual GitHub Release round trip.
Runtime is unchanged from PR185. Ponytail full extends existing fixtures instead of adding a new driver/framework. Independent exact-head review and remote execution evidence belong to the linked acceptance PR; no local heavy tests.
Local publication rejects an existing legacy data or data-empty namespace, or a data entry in remote VERSION, when output-r-data is selected. This guard runs before hooks and again while preparing all destinations, before any publication. Legacy restore remains supported; publication does not migrate or delete legacy remote data. Regression fixtures cover directory-only, empty, advertisement-only and combined legacy states. Remote verification is required before delivery. Ponytail full review reuses the existing publication preflight and preparation boundaries; no migration framework or new configuration policy is introduced.


Same: pinned projr 90be50132d16aee33e39c0f7f35ef906c35f5397 R/yml-dest.R defaults none inspection to upload-all. R/dest-send-label.R uses an empty destination filename set for none; sync planning treats every source filename as extra. Thus explicit upload-missing and sync-diff overwrite all selected files and retain extras. Sync-purge uploads/purges a nonempty source; an empty source has no known extras and does not purge. Existing non-purged destinations carry an untrusted star when their label version is updated. Cues do not suppress the blind upload of nonempty sources.
Same/different: no new default policy; file mode still defaults to sync-diff and omitted inspection still means the not-yet-supported manifest mode, which fails before hooks. Existing corrections for newly empty metadata remain. Source CSV capture, guarded path/type checks and the physical installer still validate bytes; none suppresses comparison-based decisions, not all filesystem reads/hashing.
Tests: all four explicit strategies plus omitted strategy, both cues, repeated same-byte builds, actual configured local restore, exact final bytes/trust markers; existing/new empty sources retain unknown extras or advertise emptiness. Remote exact-head compilation/platform/API/renderer checks and independent review are required before delivery. GitHub publication, manifest comparison and archive history remain pending. Ponytail full reuses the existing action planner and guarded installer; one flag and explicit effective transfer selection avoid a second storage engine or speculative transport abstraction.



Same: pinned projr 90be50132d16aee33e39c0f7f35ef906c35f5397 R/remote-versions.R409 requires recorded label/version rows remotely and matching project history; R/dest-send-label.R333 selects history comparison or physical fallback. Omitted inspection now executes that existing default. Explicit upload-all ignores comparison. Existing invalid CSV/VERSION history remains an error before any destination changes, rather than being discarded in a fallback.
Different/bug correction: the source helper at R/remote-versions.R608 strips the untrusted star before manifest eligibility. Rust preserves its meaning: a starred label falls back to file comparison. Duplicate/ambiguous selected rows also fall back. Matching history is not authentication or a guarantee that actual remote bytes have not independently drifted.
Implementation/tests: reuse physical staging/rollback guards while applying history-selected actions; unselected actual bytes survive partial sync-diff, whereas sync-purge still replaces the entire set. Actual default/explicit-mode build fixtures exercise matching history, deliberate byte drift, partial updates, unchanged cue retention, starred/missing/mismatched/duplicate history fallback. Physical source/destination inspection still protects staging and concurrent changes during a transfer; no zero-read guarantee. Ponytail full adds one shared compared-transfer entry point rather than a second installer. All remote exact-head gates and independent review remain required. Archive, configured GitHub publication and full remote compatibility remain pending.
Review-driven coverage extends trusted history to all four strategies and both cues with actual configured restore, including remote byte drift and unrecorded extras. An unrecorded file/directory shape conflict must fail before destination or metadata changes, preserving the successful local release for inspection.



Same: pinned projr R/dest-send-label.R390 uses cue/current-target existence, continuous unchanged project history, and newest catalog/VERSION/manifest agreement to select an eligible older comparison. R/manifest.R253 stops reuse across an intervening change, even when contents later revert. Archive is the existing default; complete version directories and empty variants coexist with shared CSV/VERSION/changelog at the pre-root. None/upload-all ignore historical comparison. Sync-purge reuploads nonempty unchanged content as before.
Different/bug correction: every newly required archive is a full source snapshot, rather than applying an older comparison’s partial changed-file plan to an absent version directory. This prevents incomplete archives after physical drift. Starred metadata stays untrusted, as documented for latest. Existing snapshots, including forward versions, remain untouched; ambiguous current numeric spellings fail before external publication. Configured append-label:false remains explicit unsupported behavior, not a claim of full local/remote parity.
Tests cover all inspection/strategy/cue combinations with exact snapshot bytes and configured restore, default archive+manifest, unchanged and changed/empty/reverted histories, star/mismatch/forward/drift evidence and prior-snapshot preservation. Ponytail full reuses numeric catalog validation, recorded CSV comparison, transfer and finalisation rather than introducing a second archive engine. No dependencies, schema changes, local heavy tests or live user-data mutations. Exact-head remote CI and independent review are required; GitHub configured publication remains open.
Independent review found that an older empty marker could be reused under manifest inspection without checking physical emptiness. The shared eligibility path now rejects nonempty historical empty markers for file and manifest modes; the regression preserves their unexpected bytes, remote metadata and local release.



Same: pinned remote-github.R740 merges selected files into label ZIPs and uploads through the Release transport; ordinary flat archive names and native metadata members use the existing helpers. None defaults upload-all without historical comparison. Reuse REST, ZIP writer/extractor, CSV and version helpers; freeze Git origin/API/token/tag before hooks using existing credential mechanisms.
Implemented subset: archive plus explicit none/upload-all (explicit/default), both cues, content and prefix/append-label naming. All target ZIPs stage before HTTP mutations. Data precedes shared CSV/VERSION/changelog; prior history and archive assets survive. Missing Releases use existing normal published creation. New empty archives carry projr-empty and advertise the current version.
Boundaries: existing current-version data, portable aliases and legacy data ambiguity fail before upload. Latest/configured data replacement/other decisions remain missing. Metadata replacement can be partially applied; preserve local release, skip bump and report uncertainty. Metadata archives are limited to 128 MiB each. No new registry, schema, credentials or access grants.
Tests: actual build through mock REST then configured restore, two-build old archive preservation, exact ZIP members, metadata replacement, partial failure, empty/preview behavior, unsupported controls, current-version and alias rejection. No live GitHub test or local heavy execution. Ponytail full reuses existing transport/ZIP/history helpers, no new dependency or parallel storage engine. Exact-head remote gates and independent review are required before delivery.
Non-public API origins require an explicit environment token. Default github.com Git/gh credential helpers are only used for the standard HTTPS api.github.com origin (port443), never forwarded to Enterprise/custom hosts. A regression uses a fake public helper and verifies it is not invoked for a loopback API.
Independent review corrections: reject numeric-equivalent full/empty current assets (including leading-zero/padded spellings) before mutation; compare distinct legacy/canonical stems before treating prior prefixed append-label:false R-data archives as legacy; reject all-space Release titles before hooks. Fixtures preserve alias bytes/no-POST/no-DELETE and complete two such R-data builds. Cleanup failures include the private retained path. Public helper credentials never cross API origins.
