title: Inspect local remote versions
text:
Current source work: ordinary local latest/archive inspection. This command does not upload, restore, verify artifact bytes or change configured remote definitions. It is separate from CAS and the deferred registry design.
Paths relative to the command’s selected project root are supported. Use physical paths: symlinked parents, candidate directories and VERSION files are rejected. No active project config, Git credentials or remote account are required.
Archive is the default layout: base/label/version directories. Numeric versions sort newest first, including empty variants. The actual directory path is retained even when version spellings differ. Multiple spellings or full/empty variants remain visible rather than silently selecting one for restore. Unrelated names are skipped; malformed numeric-looking version names and special candidates fail.
Latest reads the exact label entry from base/VERSION. It reports the trailing asterisk as metadata_untrusted, plus present and empty fields. A missing target is reported explicitly; an absent asterisk is not proof of verified content. Archive results do not infer trust from metadata and return null for that field. An absent base or VERSION yields no entries and creates nothing. Duplicate label entries and malformed advertised versions are errors.
Use –path-append-label false only when version directories or latest contents are directly at the supplied base. VERSION remains at that explicit base. For latest, reading that file means the base already exists, so present is true and empty is false: a sibling base-empty is not selected. This mode does not infer whether the base contains data files; directory presence is not integrity. This makes the inspected path explicit; it is not a new remote registry format.
Machine output retains protocol v1 and adds a versions query result. No byte verification, latest-source selection, credential discovery or publication occurs.

title: Inspect local remote versions
text:
Download one ordinary local version
Current source work adds remote download. It is an explicit transfer, independent of configured source selection and build publication. For archive, supply the exact numeric directory spelling via –remote-version (for example v1.2.3-4). For latest, omit that option: the advertised VERSION label entry is required. A full archive directory wins over its corresponding -empty variant.
proj --project . remote download --path /physical/archive --label raw-data --remote-version v1.2.3 --destination downloaded-data
proj --project . remote download --path /physical/latest --label raw-data --structure latest --destination downloaded-data
The destination parent must exist. Private staging receives all source files (including nested and hidden files) before an existing destination changes. Matching files receive downloaded bytes; destination-only files survive by default. –clear explicitly discards those extras only after staging succeeds. An empty source marker preserves existing files normally, or produces an empty destination with –clear. A marker containing entries is rejected.
Project-root/ancestor, VCS/framework-state and overlapping destinations are rejected, along with symlinked paths and linked/special copied entries. Hard-linked external aliases keep their bytes. Copy/selection failure preserves the existing destination. If installation fails, restoration is attempted; a failed rollback reports where the original directory was retained. This is not crash atomicity or protection against concurrent writers. Post-install cleanup failure is reported as an installed download with incomplete private-staging cleanup.
The command does not authenticate metadata, compare downloaded bytes to CSV, choose configured restore sources or change local VERSION/manifest/configuration. A latest untrusted marker does not prevent this explicitly requested download; it remains a warning about metadata, not a verified-content claim. Machine mode returns completed: true only after successful completion.
Permission flags are preserved for newly downloaded entries. Merge mode retains existing file/directory permission flags, and an existing destination root keeps its flags even with –clear. Ownership, ACLs and extended attributes are outside this bounded guarantee; replacing a tree is not a full metadata-preserving backup.

title: Inspect local remote versions
section: Inspect and apply a concrete local file policy
text:
Inspect and apply a concrete local file policy
Current source work adds remote store for file-inspected transfers to one explicit physical target. This is the file-policy layer, not configured build publication or archive/version metadata management. Supply –inspect file explicitly; manifest/none inspection are not accepted by this bounded command. The existing configuration default inspection is unchanged.
proj --machine --project . remote store --source generated --destination /physical/remote/output/v1.2.3 --inspect file --dry-run
proj --project . remote store --source generated --destination /physical/remote/output/v1.2.3 --inspect file --strategy sync-diff
The default strategy is sync-diff, matching projr. upload-all selects every source file and keeps destination-only files; upload-missing uploads only absent names; sync-diff uploads new/different files and removes destination-only files; sync-purge lists all existing files for removal and every source file for upload. A dry run reports uploads, overwrites, removals and same_bytes (informational even when those paths are re-uploaded). It creates nothing.
This command uses current streaming MD5 byte inventories, not modification time or a claim of authenticity. Hidden/nested files are included; empty subdirectories are not transfer records. The destination parent must exist. It stages selected source bytes, checks their hashes and rechecks source/target inventories before the shared guarded installer changes the target. Mirror execution builds a full replacement snapshot, so unchanged bytes may be copied privately too; do not interpret the plan as a syscall or disk-I/O count.
Source files stay unchanged. Retained paths of the same type keep existing permission flags; new paths use source flags. The download safeguards and limits above apply, including Windows read-only cleanup failures and partial cleanup residue. No crash/concurrent-writer isolation or ACL/ownership/xattr parity follows.
VERSION, manifest.csv, configured remotes, cue selection, historical comparison, empty remote naming and GitHub/CAS structures are untouched. Use the concrete version directory as destination; this command does not publish a complete discoverable remote snapshot by itself.
Native filename aliases (for example A.csv/a.csv on a case-insensitive target) are rejected before staging when the planned spelling differs from an existing entry. This includes directory components and keeps upload-missing from becoming an overwrite. Case-sensitive targets retain distinct names. Case-only migrations are not silently inferred by this bounded file-policy command.

title: Inspect local remote versions
section: Work with explicit GitHub Release assets
text:
Work with explicit GitHub Release assets
The source CLI provides remote github assets, remote github upload and remote github download. Each requires –repository owner/repo and –tag RELEASE_TAG. Upload also requires –source FILE and –name ASSET_NAME; –create-release explicitly permits a missing Release to be created. Existing names are rejected without deletion. Download requires –name, –destination FILE and –max-bytes N. Source/destination file paths are relative to the selected project root unless absolute. The destination parent must already exist.
Use an existing GITHUB_PAT, GH_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN, in that order. Public list and download requests can be anonymous. GITHUB_API_URL supports an explicit Enterprise API endpoint including /api/v3. Tokens are never command arguments. No authentication setup or additional credential helper is installed.
Machine assets returns result.assets; machine upload/download returns completed through the existing worker. ZIP creation/extraction, projr metadata ZIP handling and configured restore are not yet provided by these explicit asset commands. An interrupted upload can have an uncertain remote result: inspect before retry. Downloads stage complete bytes before replacement, preserve existing permissions, and reject protected project state, links and special files. No archive integrity, crash atomicity or concurrent-writer isolation claim follows.
The CLI does not initialise HTTP wire logging and its own error messages omit tokens, response bodies and signed redirect URLs. Library embedders must avoid ureq DEBUG/TRACE logging for sensitive requests because dependency logging is not redacted. Redirects remove Authorization but do not confine network access to a provider host; this transport is not a network sandbox.

title: Inspect local remote versions
section: GitHub ZIP packaging and explicit directory transfer
text:
GitHub ZIP packaging and explicit directory transfer
Current source extends the native Release transport with projr flat names: prefix-label-vVERSION.zip for archive, prefix-label.zip for latest, and -empty before .zip for empty variants. With no prefix, the label is always used, including path_append_label=false. Metadata assets remain shared and unprefixed: manifest.zip contains manifest.csv, VERSION.zip contains VERSION, and CHANGELOG.zip contains CHANGELOG.md. Directory ZIP entries are relative to the selected source, without an enclosing folder. Nonempty parent-directory entries retain Unix permission modes; empty directory entries remain omitted. Empty sources contain the single zero-byte projr-empty sentinel; empty subdirectories are not archived.
The CLI adds remote github upload-directory (label/structure/remote-version, optional prefix/path-append-label), upload-metadata (kind manifest/version/ changelog and a source directory), and download-directory (exact asset name, destination, max-bytes, max-expanded-bytes, optional clear/empty). Uploads remain new-name-only; metadata is packaged byte-for-byte rather than silently merged. Download stages extraction privately and uses the existing guarded merge/clear installer. Explicit empty requires exactly the sentinel and consumes it before installation. Destination-only files survive unless clear is requested.
Safety changes from R’s direct utils::unzip: bounded expanded bytes and100000 members, CRC validation, reject links/special/encrypted entries, traversal, backslashes, device names, native aliases, duplicate members and parent/file collisions before project installation. Retain existing installer rollback and Windows backup-cleanup limits; no crash/concurrent-writer guarantee is added.
Ponytail full: one ZIP crate with only Deflate enabled, existing MD5 inventory, HTTP client and guarded installer. No backend interface, registry or new YAML policy. Independent tests cover exact metadata/Unicode/hidden/empty members, malicious names, CRC/expanded limits and mocked actual ZIP upload/download merge/clear. No local heavy tests; remote lock resolution, exact-head platform/ pinned/docs acceptance and independent review are pending.
Pinned sources: flat names, ZIP layout, empty sentinel, metadata assets. Configured single-label restore and explicit replacement are described below. Historical metadata merging, automatic publication, credential-helper fallback and complete CAS-structure integration remain outstanding. This source candidate does not update the published/installed preview.
Review amendments share the existing native directory-entry alias guard with file-policy transfers, validate empty-directory CRC with a bounded probe, and never persist an expanded-byte probe beyond each member’s advertised size. Directory modes apply deepest-first after extraction; an existing destination’s modes still follow the previously documented merge policy. File-only ZIPs from other writers have no directory privacy metadata to restore. Source root modes are not encoded as a new manifest field. No ACL/ownership/xattr claim follows. Temporary paths are created beneath the physical canonical system temp directory; macOS /var aliases are not an excuse to weaken external path guards.
Extraction also checks actual directory spelling immediately after creation, rejecting filesystems that rewrite it rather than merging distinct Unicode members. The extracted-tree owner restores directory owner access for cleanup; explicit close reports a retained path on cleanup failure. The directory-transfer command checks extraction and transfer cleanup on success and failure and distinguishes installed output from failed transfer. Readonly/zero-mode owned directory cleanup is exercised unprivileged in the pinned gate.

title: Inspect local remote versions
text:
Explicit GitHub asset replacement
Current source adds –replace to upload, upload-directory and upload-metadata, and GithubReleaseClient::replace_asset. Default uploads still reject existing names. Explicit replacement follows the working projr delete-then-upload sequence: remote-github-httr.R554-662.
Before deletion, validate the regular source, stage its complete bytes privately, resolve the Release/unique asset and validate its trusted upload endpoint. An absent name uploads normally. A successful delete is followed by one upload; errors after deletion explicitly state that the previous asset was deleted. An interrupted deletion reports an uncertain old-asset state and does not start the upload. This is not atomic publication, backup retention or remote rollback. There is no automatic retry, new history/sealing policy or changed YAML default.
Ponytail full reuses the existing client and request/body fixtures, with a private file snapshot only for explicit replacement. Mocked end-to-end witnesses cover staged bytes despite source mutation after delete, exact DELETE/POST ordering, denied/interrupted delete, failed/malformed upload, untrusted endpoints, ambiguous names, unsafe sources and machine CLI output. These are mocked REST operations, not actual GitHub Release mutations. No live user data/credentials or local heavy tests. PR182 passed exact-head remote gates and independent review. Configured single-label restore follows below; full automatic publication remains open.

title: Inspect local remote versions
text:
Configured single-label restore
remote restore –label LABEL –max-bytes N –max-expanded-bytes N resolves one declared final directory from merged active configuration. Optional –position source/dest, –provider local/github and –title restrict lookup; –profile follows existing earlier-profile/local precedence. –remote-version selects an exact archive version; otherwise numeric newest is selected. GitHub latest reads canonical VERSION.zip, then downloads its label ZIP. –repository owner/repo avoids requiring Git; otherwise origin is inspected locally and its host must match the API. GITHUB_API_URL and existing environment tokens retain the explicit transport contract. No credentials are installed.
Existing per-directory source.local/source.github title references or named inline definitions precede eligible build.local/build.github destinations. A shared referenced definition may be refined inline through the existing deep merge (null still inherits). Destination source:false excludes it; true or a matching label preference beats the first eligible fallback. content:null/false selects nothing, true selects declared non-cache roles, and lists select declared labels. Source/provider/title declaration order is preserved. No retry switches to another configured source after lookup/download fails.
A valid root manifest.csv is required, matching projr’s prior-build gate. Labels with no recorded files and advertised empty variants skip without clearing. CSV history is not used as an integrity/trust proof. Full sources stage before the existing merge/clear installer; –clear never removes files before a source has been found and copied. Default merge preserves destination-only files. Machine results disclose restored/skipped, selected provider/title/version and destination; failures keep protocol stdout structured with static error text. Stderr carries the operational diagnostic chain, including paths and parser details; it is not a general configuration-redaction boundary. HTTP errors omit credentials and response bodies.
This deliberately fixes R source-selection indexing/inline-definition bugs and clear-before-lookup data loss. It does not add R’s implicit hard-coded archive fallback: undeclared remotes/paths are errors under the agreed explicit mapping contract. Nonempty get policy mappings fail explicitly rather than pretending that R’s ineffective get.strategy/get.conflict controls work. Send policy is not executed by restore. Definitions retain local path versus GitHub title/tag id semantics, including spaces and @version tag normalization.
Boundary: ordinary inline remote/source fields are accepted by this command’s read-only configuration projection only. Normal build validation still rejects unsupported ordinary publication fields, preventing silently ignored uploads. Configured automatic publication, cue/history policy integration, all-label default restore, complete credential-helper fallback and the issue706 registry remain subsequent work. Installed preview remains unchanged.
Pinned comparison: restore gate/selection/download, inline destination defaults, content eligibility. Ponytail full reuses merged YAML, typed core validation, CSV decoding, numeric version comparison and guarded local/ZIP installers. No backend trait, new registry or persistence schema. Filesystem and mocked REST actual CLI fixtures cover source priority, references/inline/profiles, destination preference, numeric archives, VERSION ZIP latest, clear/merge/empty and corrupt failure preservation. No actual GitHub Release mutation or local heavy test is performed. PR183 passed independent review at44478558d0ef41660d513a3f7d74fe399684b245, all12checks and the full pinned gate. It merged ascee85a164fa43cb827c0db69814199994fa4ea66 with an identical tested tree.
Configured restore uses the shared profile selection order: explicit profile, PROJR_PROFILE, QUARTO_PROFILE, then build.profile, with earlier profiles winning and local overrides last. Machine failures preserve installation/recovery details on stderr, including retained backup paths; stdout stays a structured failure. Legacy data CSV rows and remote data namespaces are read without rewriting history; ambiguous canonical/legacy namespaces fail before installation. One optional VERSION trust marker is accepted; it is not a byte-verification claim.
Review precision: VERSION.zip requires exactly the canonical VERSION member spelling, including on case-insensitive filesystems. Metadata transfer staging also closes explicitly and reports cleanup failure paths.

title: Inspect local remote versions
text:
Configured local publication candidate
Current source supports build.local archive (the default) and latest publication with manifest inspection by default, explicit file comparison, or explicit none comparison. This is newer than installed preview.2 and is not complete projr remote parity. All selected namespace identities are checked before hooks; every current CSV-selected snapshot and existing remote metadata is staged/read before the first destination changes. Data precedes manifest.csv, VERSION and an existing project CHANGELOG.md. The build’s existing irreversible publication boundary preserves the successful local release on publication failure and skips its next-dev bump; remote effects may be partial.
build:
  scripts: []
  git: false
  local:
    delivery:
      path: ../delivery
      structure: latest
      content: [output]
      send:
        inspect: file
        cue: if-change
        strategy: sync-diff
Content false/null selects nothing, true selects declared non-cache labels, and a list selects exactly those declared labels. Selected labels require CSV hash capture. Explicit label lists retain order; true uses sorted declared labels. There is no implicit role/destination and no registry706 change. Previews and output_run:false skip publication.








Control
This candidate’s execution/fixture scope
Remaining




Content true/false/null/list
Actual CLI selection fixtures; true excludes cache
Full configured provider matrix


cue if-change / always
Both against each strategy; repeated identical sync-diff tests label-version retention/advance
Archive comparison-version selection


inspect file
Shared MD5 byte inspection, current CSV snapshots, exact source-byte validation
GitHub configured inspection


inspect manifest
Default and explicit mode; matching project/remote history; physical fallback on missing/mismatched/starred history
Archive comparison and GitHub publication


inspect none
All four strategies and both cues; default upload-all; exact build/store/restore bytes and trust markers
Other providers/layouts


upload-all
Upload all selected files, retain extras; existing remote marked untrusted
Other inspection modes


upload-missing
Preserve existing names/bytes, add missing; changes to existing remote marked untrusted
Other inspection modes


sync-diff
Add/change/remove; no-change cue fixture
Archive/history interaction


sync-purge
Mirror full selected file set, including same-byte files, matching the pinned source quirk
Other inspection modes



if-change, sync-diff and manifest inspection remain the existing defaults. Nonempty get controls, send.conflict and title-level cue are not silently accepted as working policy. path-append-label:false is explicitly deferred here because its full destination contains the shared metadata namespace.
History retains prior label/version rows and replaces current label/version rows with the current project CSV rows. Upload modes can intentionally preserve extra or old bytes, so desired-source CSV history is not proof that those bytes equal the remote; the VERSION asterisk discloses untrusted existing state.
Two source defects are corrected explicitly: newly empty latest labels receive an advertised VERSION entry, and file-equal sync-diff repairs missing/starred label metadata after inspection. Pinned R latest/file returns the project version without checking VERSION (.dsl_gr_gvc_latest_file); its no-change branch can otherwise leave the directory undiscoverable or stale-marked. This is a bounded metadata/discoverability correction, not a new default cue or trust policy.
Ponytail full shares the existing definition/content parser, numeric version validation, CSV format and four-strategy actions/guarded installer. Snapshots preserve selected source directory modes and all staging trees get explicit cleanup on success/failure. Planned missing-path namespaces use conservative portable case/NFC comparison; actual native spelling is rechecked before installation. No ownership/ACL/xattr, crash atomicity or concurrent-writer isolation claim. No actual GitHub Release test mutation or local heavy testing. Remote exact-head checks and independent review are required before delivery.
When publishing output-r-data, an existing legacy data/data-empty namespace or data entry in remote VERSION is rejected. Restore can still read legacy data; publication does not rename, delete or migrate it. Choose a separate destination until an explicit migration is supported.

No comparison during configured local publication
Set send.inspect to none to make planning ignore comparison hashes/history. The default strategy then becomes upload-all; both cues still upload nonempty sources. Explicit upload-missing and sync-diff also blindly overwrite selected filenames and retain remote-only files, matching projr rather than their file-inspected behavior. Existing destinations are marked untrusted with a star.
Explicit sync-purge replaces the entire file set when the source is nonempty. With an empty source it retains unknown remote extras: without comparison, projr does not discover extras to trigger a purge. New empty destinations are still advertised. These combinations are covered by actual CLI build/store/restore fixtures, including repeated same-byte builds and both cues.
None controls comparison decisions; guarded path/type checks, source CSV-byte validation, staging and physical installation safety still read files. It is not a promise of zero remote reads or hashing. The shared physical transfer remains guarded and may read destination bytes while installing. Archive and configured GitHub publication remain pending.


Manifest comparison for local latest publication
Manifest is the default inspection. The remote label VERSION must be unstarred, and the corresponding label/version CSV rows must exist and match project history exactly as filename/MD5 sets. Then current source rows are compared with those recorded rows. Otherwise comparison falls back to physical files. Missing, mismatched, duplicate or ambiguous rows cannot establish trust; malformed history still fails closed rather than being overwritten.
A matching history is a performance/decision trust convention, not proof of actual remote bytes. If bytes drift independently while history still agrees, unselected files are retained. Use inspect: file to compare actual bytes. Sync-purge still replaces the whole file set when triggered. Shared guarded staging checks physical paths/types/bytes during installation; this mode does not promise zero remote reads. Explicit upload-all ignores comparison like projr.
Projr strips the star before its latest-manifest helper checks history. Rust deliberately treats a starred label as untrusted and falls back to file comparison, consistent with the stated marker meaning. This is a source bug correction, not a new history/authenticity policy. Archive and configured GitHub publication are still pending.


Configured ordinary local archives
Omitting structure uses archive, matching projr. Each label stores complete snapshots at path/label/vVERSION (or vVERSION-empty), with shared metadata at path. Earlier versions are retained. Explicit path-append-label:false remains unsupported for configured publication; source lookup/explicit download support is separate.
For if-change, an older archive can be reused only when its newest catalog entry, unstarred VERSION label and matching project/remote history agree, and the version falls within the continuous unchanged suffix of project history. File inspection then compares that eligible directory’s bytes; manifest inspection compares its recorded rows. Missing/stale/future/mismatched/untrusted evidence forces the current version. Always with an absent current destination selects a fresh snapshot. None and upload-all do not select historical comparisons.
When a new snapshot is required it contains the complete current CSV-selected source, including when only one file differed from an older comparison. This avoids the native source’s potential partial-new-directory behavior after old comparison byte drift. Old snapshots are never patched as comparison sources. Shared metadata still advances when unchanged content reuses an older version. Empty transitions retain history; redundant unchanged empty snapshots are skipped.
Remote fixtures cover the 3 inspection x 4 strategy x 2 cue matrix through actual build/store/restore, default archive/manifest, empty transitions, reversion after an intervening change, and missing/untrusted/forward/drifted comparison evidence. Archive root/container identities and catalogs are validated before hooks; exact current-version spelling is checked during all-target preparation before any destination applies. No remote transaction or concurrent-writer guarantee. Configured GitHub publication and CAS policy remain separate.


Configured GitHub publication candidate
Current source adds a bounded build.github path:
build:
  git: false
  scripts: []
  github:
    data:
      content: [output]
      send: {inspect: none}
Archive is the existing structure default; none inspection defaults upload-all. Both cues upload selected nonempty bytes without historical comparison. Archive data uses native label-vVERSION.zip or label-vVERSION-empty.zip names and the existing prefix/append-label naming. Missing Releases are created as normal published Releases, not drafts. Use a dedicated destination for testing.
Git origin selects owner/repository; existing API URL and credentials are captured before hooks. No credentials are installed or changed. Current CSV-selected bytes stream into restorable ZIPs; all targets stage before the first upload. Existing CSV/VERSION history is retained. Data precedes manifest.zip, VERSION.zip and an existing project CHANGELOG.zip. Metadata ZIPs require exactly the canonical member; shared metadata and existing data download/extraction are bounded at 128 MiB compressed and expanded per archive; selected merge extraction has the same expanded limit. These caps fail during preparation before remote changes.
Set structure: latest to replace label.zip (or label-empty.zip). Archive remains the default and may replace only the exact canonical current-version asset; older versions remain untouched. Existing data ZIPs are downloaded and validated, then selected CSV bytes overwrite their matching members while remote-only files survive. Empty source selection leaves existing data intact; the strategy table below explains when label VERSION also advances. Upload-all, upload-missing and sync-diff updates to existing targets receive a starred VERSION because retained extras are not described by the source inventory. A nonempty sync-purge replaces the complete file set and removes that star. Project/history metadata still advances. Empty-to-full upload removes the validated obsolete empty variant only after the full upload succeeds.
Catalog case/numeric aliases, simultaneous full/empty assets, malformed ZIPs and legacy data ambiguity fail during all-target preparation before upload/deletion. File/manifest GitHub inspection remains pending. Data and shared metadata replacement use non-atomic delete-then-upload: failure may leave partial state or a missing asset. The successful local release survives and next-dev bump is skipped. No remote rollback, automatic retry or concurrent-writer isolation claim.
Evidence uses actual CLI build/store/restore against loopback mocked REST, including Release creation, ZIP members, metadata replacement, old archive retention, latest replacement/restore with retained extras, both cues, empty-source preservation, validated empty transitions, partial failure and preflight rejection. This is not a live GitHub Release round trip. Installed preview unchanged; remote CI/review required.
Non-public API origins require an explicit environment token. Default github.com Git/gh credential helpers are only used for the standard HTTPS api.github.com origin (port443), never forwarded to Enterprise/custom hosts. A regression uses a fake public helper and verifies it is not invoked for a loopback API.
Public gh credential fallback explicitly requests –hostname github.com, so an inherited GH_HOST cannot select Enterprise credentials for the public API. Numeric archive alias checks remove exactly one generated .zip suffix, preserving valid prefixes/labels that themselves end in .zip. Regression fixtures cover both.


GitHub no-inspection strategy controls
With explicit send.inspect: none, the default strategy is upload-all. All four strategies are supported with either cue and latest/archive layout:








Strategy
Nonempty source against existing target
Empty source against existing target




upload-all
Upload every selected file; retain extras
Keep data and label VERSION


upload-missing
Same blind upload as upload-all
Keep data and label VERSION


sync-diff
Same blind upload as upload-all
Keep data; advance untrusted label VERSION


sync-purge
Replace complete data file set
Keep data and label VERSION



These are pinned projr’s none-inspection interactions: no comparison means every source file is considered extra, so missing/diff cannot skip existing matching paths or infer destination-only files. Neither cue changes that fact. Nonempty purge knows the complete replacement and produces an unstarred label VERSION. Empty source cannot infer destination extras, even under purge/always. New targets (including empty targets) remain discoverable as described above.
Mock REST fixtures execute all 2 layouts x 4 strategies x 2 cues through actual build and configured restore with exact ZIP/metadata/retained-extra assertions; empty-source coverage checks all strategies and cues. This is not live GitHub evidence. File/manifest inspection and historical archive comparison remain pending.

title: proj ignore
text:
Commands for interacting with tracking file exclusions, handling operations to manually or automatically modify .gitignore and .Rbuildignore files.


Manually appends one or more raw file or directory paths to the project ignore files.
Unlike automatic configurations driven by _proj.yml, these manual entries represent permanent, user-specified exclusions and are placed strictly above the # --- PROJ MANAGED --- blocks.



<PATHS>...: One or more raw file or directory paths to be ignored.
--force-create: Boolean flag (default true). If true, creates ignore files if they don’t exist. If false, skips file creation unless inherently warranted by environmental cues (e.g. finding a .git folder or a DESCRIPTION file).
--type: Optional filter selection (all [default], git, rbuild). Determines which tracking surface receives the manual path entries. Note that .Rbuildignore is skipped entirely if no DESCRIPTION file exists at the project root.





Manually forces paths to be tracked by appending negated syntax (e.g. !path/ or ^!pattern$).
These unignore entries represent permanent, user-specified negations and are placed strictly below the # --- END PROJ MANAGED --- boundary in .gitignore and .Rbuildignore files.



<PATHS>...: One or more raw file or directory paths to force tracking.
--type: Optional filter selection (all [default], git, rbuild). Determines which tracking surface receives the negated entries. Note that .Rbuildignore is skipped entirely if no DESCRIPTION file exists at the project root.





The library core automatically synchronizes ignore rules dynamically across .gitignore and .Rbuildignore based on the configuration of _proj.yml.

Note: While the automated ignore synchronization is invoked implicitly by the CLI via commands like proj yml read (and acts seamlessly under the hood), the ignore subcommand namespace exists openly to support explicit manual additions via proj ignore add.




The tool automatically locates the project boundaries via a heuristic upward path traversal. It begins checking from the user’s current working directory upward: - It discovers the conceptual root by finding a directory containing a VERSION file. - It continues upward through up to 5 directory levels seeking an optimal foundational root confirming the presence of either _proj.yml or a .git tracking context alongside the VERSION.



The tool targets specifically two core exception list files: - .gitignore (safeguards git commit environments) - .Rbuildignore (safeguards strict CRAN environments and rbuild processes)
Based on the individual block ignore settings within _proj.yml (e.g. ignore: all), properties are intelligently resolved as standard git glob patterns and Rbuild regex match patterns appropriately.



Modifications made by the tool into .gitignore and .Rbuildignore are safely strictly demarcated with protected slice logic block comments. This preserves user-defined modifications outside the managed span: - Operations scan for # --- PROJ MANAGED --- and # --- END PROJ MANAGED ---. - Targeted slice elements are swapped or appended into existing scopes only between these exact markers. - If the boundary blocks are absent, the tool automatically injects them natively at the base end.

title: Install the development preview
text:
WarningTry it on a disposable project



Use sample data or a disposable copy of your project. Production builds (proj build) can modify or remove files. Recovery covers only recorded managed paths. Never run production builds on the only copy of important work. Previews are not a security sandbox; code you run can still change files.

title: Install the development preview
text:
Choose the preview explicitly
The published v0.4.0-preview.2 is an early development release. These instructions pin that version. The release passed the integrated analysis, renderer and archive checks. Both platform downloads were checked against the tagged source and their checksums. See delivery evidence.
GitHub’s stable Latest release is still v0.3.0; it does not contain the current preview features or the new binary-delivery metadata.







Download
Requirements




Linux / WSL Ubuntu
x86-64 processor, glibc 2.35 or newer; Bash, curl and sha256sum or shasum. Ubuntu 22.04 or newer meets the glibc requirement; user-local installation was verified in WSL Ubuntu 24.04.


Windows
x86-64 processor; use PowerShell 7 (pwsh) for the installer below.


macOS / ARM
No binaries supplied for this preview.



You do not need Git, Rust, Cargo or administrator access to install these binaries. The Python tutorial additionally needs Python 3. Other analysis tools are needed only if your own scripts or reports use them.

title: Install the development preview
text:
Ubuntu and WSL Ubuntu
Run this inside Ubuntu, not in a Windows terminal. Check that uname -m reports x86_64 and getconf GNU_LIBC_VERSION reports glibc 2.35 or newer.
mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/bin"
installer="$(mktemp)"
curl -fsSL "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/768da1bf1b83be83b657b36219f299f37130ba03/install-local.sh" -o "$installer" &&
  PROJ_RELEASE_VERSION=0.4.0-preview.2 \
  PROJ_INSTALL_DIR="$HOME/.local/bin" bash "$installer"
rm -f "$installer"
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
hash -r
proj --version
Expected version: proj 0.4.0-preview.2.
The script comes from the reviewed source commit. It downloads the pinned Linux binary, checks its SHA256 against the release manifest, and installs it as ~/.local/bin/proj. It replaces an existing proj in that folder only after verification succeeds. No sudo or local compilation is involved.

title: Install the development preview
text:
Windows
Open PowerShell 7 (pwsh) as your normal user:
$installDir = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE ".local\bin"
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $installDir | Out-Null
$installer = Join-Path ([IO.Path]::GetTempPath()) ("proj-install-" + [guid]::NewGuid() + ".ps1")
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/768da1bf1b83be83b657b36219f299f37130ba03/install.ps1" -OutFile $installer
$env:PROJ_RELEASE_VERSION = "0.4.0-preview.2"
$env:PROJ_INSTALL_DIR = $installDir
& $installer
Remove-Item -LiteralPath $installer
$env:Path = "$installDir;$env:Path"
proj --version
Expected version: proj 0.4.0-preview.2.
The script checks the Windows binary’s SHA256 before installing proj.exe in $HOME\.local\bin. It does not change system settings or require an administrator terminal. This installer is checked with PowerShell 7; these instructions do not claim Windows PowerShell 5.1 compatibility.

title: Install the development preview
text:
Finding the command later
The PATH lines above make the command available in the current terminal. In a new terminal, repeat that PATH line or add the installation folder to your own user PATH. The installer does not make that permanent change for you.
Another program can also be named proj. Check command -v proj in Ubuntu or Get-Command proj in PowerShell, then proj --version, if you see unexpected help or results.

title: Install the development preview
text:
What the checksum proves
The installer requires the release’s version.txt and exactly one matching entry in checksums.txt. A missing or incorrect checksum stops installation before the existing binary is replaced. For a manual download, use sha256sum on Linux or Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 in PowerShell and compare the result with the manifest’s exact filename entry before running it.
The manifest comes from the same GitHub release. Checksums detect corruption and mismatches; they are not independent signatures or proof of a reproducible build. The release also includes source-commit.txt and version.txt. The reviewed source is 768da1bf1b83be83b657b36219f299f37130ba03.

title: Install the development preview
text:
Start small
Follow Run your first analysis with sample data. Broad M1/M2 milestones, R/IDE parity, complete input/code/dependency provenance, and reliable analysis-free publication retries remain unfinished. Preview recovery is bounded: it does not isolate every write or undo arbitrary external effects.
See what works, detailed preview status and verified delivery notes for the evidence and limits.
